items.title: FG Targets 25,000 Free Cataract Surgeries by 2027
items.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has announced plans to perform 25,000 free cataract surgeries across the country by the end of 2027 as part of efforts to reduce avoidable blindness and expand access to quality eye care. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at an event marking the 2026 World Sight Day. Salako, who was represented by the Director of e-Health Division, Mrs Doris Afam-Aneke, said the initiative was part of the government’s Renewed Hope Health Connect programme aimed at restoring sight and improving the quality of life of Nigerians. “As part of our Renewed Hope Health Connect, we’re embarking on performing 25,000 free cataract surgeries across the country by the end of 2027. This target is ambitious, but it is achievable. “More importantly, it represents our determination to restore sight, independence, productivity and hope to thousands of Nigerians whose lives can be transformed through timely surgical intervention,” he said. To improve access to eye care, Salako said the government had activated more than 1,400 primary healthcare centres (PHCs) nationwide to provide essential eye care services. He added that more than 3,000 healthcare workers had been trained across 16 states to strengthen the prevention, early detection and management of common eye conditions at the community level. According to him, integrating primary eye care into the primary healthcare system remained a key strategy for bringing essential services closer to the people, particularly those in underserved communities. “A major pillar of our eye health strategy has been the integration and expansion of primary eye care services across the country. The evidence is clear. “Sustainable progress in eye health can only be achieved when services are available at the point closest to the people. This is why government has prioritised the strengthening of primary healthcare systems as the foundation for delivering essential eye care interventions,” he said. The minister further disclosed that the government had distributed more than 1.5 million pairs of prescription spectacles to Nigerians in 16 states through the Effective Spectacle Coverage Initiative, known as Jigi-Bola 2.0. He said preparations were at an advanced stage to extend the initiative to 10 additional states to improve access to affordable vision correction for people with uncorrected refractive errors. Salako also revealed that more than 1.5 million school-age children had been screened for visual problems through the school eye health programme, with those requiring treatment referred to appropriate health facilities. He added that the government planned to establish four additional vision centres in Enugu, Edo, Sokoto and Nasarawa states to strengthen secondary eye care services, improve referral systems and expand access to specialised treatment. The minister said the interventions were designed to ensure that Nigerians could access essential eye care services regardless of their location or financial circumstances. He identified the key components of the National Eye Care Commitment as integrating primary eye care into PHCs, expanding access to ready-made spectacles through Jigi-Bola 2.0, improving cataract surgical coverage, strengthening the eye health workforce and removing barriers to eye care. Salako also announced that Nigeria would co-host the first-ever Global Summit on Eye Health, scheduled for November 2 in Antigua and Barbuda. He described the summit as an opportunity to strengthen international collaboration and advance the integration of eye health into universal health coverage. He said Nigeria’s participation would place the country at the centre of international health diplomacy efforts to integrate eye care into universal health coverage. “No nation can attain its full potential when millions of its citizens face avoidable barriers to seeing, learning, working and thriving. This recognition continues to guide our commitment to strengthening eye health services within the broader framework of the Renewed Hope Agenda,” he said. Earlier, the National Coordinator of the National Eye, Ear and Sensory Functions Health Programme, Dr Oteri Okolo Eme, said more than 80 per cent of visual impairment in Nigeria was avoidable, making the integration of primary eye care into the primary healthcare system a strategic priority. Eme said the government had established a network of national master trainers across the six geopolitical zones and trained about 4,000 primary healthcare workers, while more than 2,200 others had received specialised training in primary eye care. She added that state-level trainers and facilitators had also been trained to support the expansion of eye care services nationwide. The coordinator disclosed that the government was developing protocols for newborn eye screening to facilitate the early detection and treatment of conditions that could cause visual impairment. “We are protecting our children and future generations. We are in the process of developing protocols for newborn screening because we believe that if we detect causes of visual impairment early, we will be able to address them and ensure better outcomes. “We are also tackling national priority eye conditions by developing standardised guidelines,” she said. Eme said the forthcoming Global Summit on Eye Health would provide an opportunity to examine the state of eye health and push for accelerated action. She called on governments, development partners, the private sector, healthcare workers, teachers, the media and Nigerians to support efforts to improve eye health. She urged governments to make dedicated budgetary allocations for eye care and encouraged Nigerians to undergo regular eye examinations to protect their sight. Also speaking, the Executive Secretary of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities, Chief Ayuba Gufwan, said investment in eye health was an investment in people. He noted that supporting persons with visual impairment and ensuring accessible eye care services would improve their participation in education, employment and community life. Similarly, the Chief Medical Director of the National Eye Centre, Kaduna, Dr Amina Hassan Wali, called for stronger partnerships, increased public awareness, early presentation for eye problems, regular eye examinations and sustained investment in eye health. “Let us work together to ensure that no one is left behind and that everyone can enjoy the gift of sight. Let us all love our eyes and make eye health a priority,” she said. The event featured the unveiling of the National Eye Health Commitments in alignment with the forthcoming Global Summit on Eye Health. items.title: PM Shehbaz condemns fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reiterates commitment to kingdom's security under Makkah pact
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday condemned recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to the Gulf state’s “sovereignty, territorial integrity and security” under the Makkah Defence Alliance. The defence pact , of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. In a post on X, the premier condemned attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport, noting that the attacks had resulted in civilian casualties. He also commended the “vigilance and professionalism” of the Saudi armed forces and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen for intercepting ballistic missiles. PM Shehbaz expressed “unwavering” solidarity with Saudi Arabia. “In line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, and recent decisions taken by its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, our commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security is resolute,” he said, adding that Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia’s right to self-defence. He called on the Houthis to immediately cease attacks. “We will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia in the face of these threats.” On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that they had struck the Saudi capital’s main international airport with a ballistic missile, in the latest attack on the kingdom claimed by the group. The attacks came after the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on the kingdom and are targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high. On Wednesday, Saudi authorities said three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports, including in the capital, Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs. For its part, a Saudi-led coalition that backs pro-government forces in Yemen said on X that it “destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform” used in the attack on Riyadh. The Houthis, who control most of the country’s northwest, are battling for territory against the Saudi-backed forces after the civil war reignited in July and they captured swathes of coastal land. Yemen’s internationally recognised government this week declared a major counter-offensive and said Houthi fighters were pushed out of strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha. But the Houthis say they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground. Against this backdrop, Pakistan has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia. On October 5, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance in Riyadh. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and was asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, to which he said both Turkiye and Pakistan had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations. On September 18, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”. Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries. At the same time, Pakistan has also asserted that the alliance is intended for collective deterrence and is defensive in nature.

items.title: Ezekwesili urges African youths to reclaim political power
items.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja Former Minister of Education, Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili, has urged Nigerian and African youths to harness their collective political power to overcome money-driven politics, demand accountable leadership and shape the continent’s future. Ezekwesili made the call on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 #FixPolitics Africa Conference, themed “Reimagining Elections in Africa: Restoring Citizens as the True Owners of Power.” She said citizens could weaken the influence of money in politics by recognising their collective strength, participating actively in elections and holding elected officials accountable for good governance. The former minister acknowledged that money had become a major influence in Nigeria’s political process but argued that its power could diminish when citizens collectively rejected poor governance and demanded leadership that served their interests. “Somebody can say, oh, you’re not being realistic. I mean, how do you fight money of the kind that we have seen in our politics? But it turns out that it comes to a time when money no longer works. “We’ve seen it in other countries. There have been countries where citizens woke up one day and said, okay, you all can have all the money, but we’re tired of being poorly governed,” she said. Ezekwesili said the conference was designed to help citizens recognise and unlock their collective power by exercising their democratic rights and using the electoral process to influence political leadership. She, however, cautioned against limiting citizens’ participation in governance to election periods, stressing that the demand for accountable leadership must continue long after votes had been cast. According to her, elections represent only a moment in the democratic process, while achieving good governance requires a sustained movement driven by citizens’ continuous engagement with those in power. “The day of election is a moment. Being governed and governed well requires a movement because it requires permanent engagement. It is not a periodic thing. It is not an episodic thing,” she said. She urged Nigerians to remain vigilant after elections and consistently demand accountability from elected officials, adding that those who desired the freedom to prosper and live in an environment that supported productivity must take an active interest in how they were governed. Citing former United States President Thomas Jefferson’s observation that “eternal vigilance is the price of freedom,” Ezekwesili said citizens must be prepared to demand the governance they desire. “If you don’t demand for it, nobody supplies it. You won’t get out of elections,” she said. Addressing concerns about alleged attempts by powerful individuals to manipulate the electoral process, Ezekwesili urged citizens not to be intimidated by those wielding political or financial influence. She maintained that sovereignty ultimately rested with the people, expressing confidence that growing political consciousness among citizens would strengthen their ability to influence Nigeria’s leadership and democratic future. “I’ve been talking to my fellow citizens. I’m encouraging my citizens to remember that Nigeria belongs to all of us. And sovereignty belongs to the people,” she said. She added that political circumstances were not permanent, warning Nigerians against assuming that existing power structures would remain unchanged. Also speaking, the Chairman of Bigs Politics Hub, Frank Nweke, said the organisation considered it its responsibility to mobilise citizens and provide platforms for discussions on issues affecting the country. Nweke said the initiative sought to raise public consciousness, encourage electoral participation and promote sustained civic engagement as part of efforts to strengthen democracy. “Everyone’s affected, right? And so we also feel a sense of responsibility to really organise, mobilise, have some of these conversations, again towards achieving one’s wishes, to arouse the consciousness of our people,” he said. He urged Nigerians to recognise that strengthening the country’s democratic process required the collective efforts of citizens, rather than the actions of political leaders alone. Similarly, the Executive Director of Fix Politics Africa, Anthony Ubani, said the conference had evolved over the past four years from an annual platform for political discussions into an initiative seeking to establish a broader civic movement across Africa. Ubani said the organisers had recognised the limitations of holding annual conferences without concrete mechanisms to implement resolutions and translate discussions into meaningful change. He explained that the fourth edition was therefore focused on moving beyond periodic gatherings to building a movement capable of taking recommendations to communities, states, countries and relevant institutions across the continent. “This year, we have thought deeply and considered that it’s important to just move from having a moment of the Africa Conference every year to have a transition into a movement,” Ubani said. He disclosed that the conference featured a roundtable involving thinkers and experts from different African countries who examined challenges facing the continent and developed recommendations for addressing them. According to him, the discussions generated what he described as “very germane ideas”, prompting the organisers to establish a small think tank to follow up on the recommendations and drive their implementation. Ubani said the objective was to ensure that the conference produced tangible results rather than ending with discussions, adding that the organisers hoped to demonstrate measurable progress when participants reconvened for the 2027 Africa Conference. items.title: South Africa withdraws asylum directive after xenophobic clashes
items.description: The South African government has withdrawn a directive on processing asylum applications following xenophobic clashes between foreign nationals and anti-immigration protesters that left vehicles burnt and foreign-owned shops looted. The Department of Home Affairs announced the withdrawal on Friday, saying the directive had triggered “serious consequences” and overwhelmed refugee reception offices within days. The department said its officials had been placed at risk and that serious threats to public safety and order had emerged, adding that it would begin a fresh process. The directive had required refugee reception offices to process asylum applications following a Constitutional Court ruling that certain procedural barriers facing asylum seekers were unconstitutional. The move prompted hundreds of people to visit refugee reception offices, reigniting tensions over immigration and the presence of foreign nationals in the country. Violence erupted on Thursday in Soweto, Johannesburg, and Durban, a port city on South Africa’s east coast, following protests organised by anti-illegal immigration groups. In Durban, at least 14 vehicles were set ablaze and a municipal building was set on fire. Police said three foreign nationals were arrested for allegedly assaulting a South African protester. In Soweto, at least 10 vehicles were torched, while small convenience stores were looted. South Africa, the continent’s wealthiest nation, has long attracted migrants from other African countries but has experienced periodic outbreaks of xenophobic violence over nearly two decades. The violence has sometimes been fuelled by disputed claims that foreign nationals take jobs and scarce resources from South African citizens. Tensions over illegal immigration have intensified ahead of local government elections scheduled for November 4, with unemployment above 30 per cent remaining a major concern. At least four foreign nationals were killed in violence earlier this year, according to South African police, although some African governments reported a higher death toll. The latest tensions have also prompted foreign nationals to leave the country. Those who departed in earlier waves of violence included citizens of Zimbabwe, Malawi, Ghana, Kenya, Lesotho, Mozambique, Nigeria and Uganda. Some were repatriated by their governments, raising diplomatic tensions with Pretoria. AFP The post South Africa withdraws asylum directive after xenophobic clashes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Malaysia closes schools in capital, parts of country due to haze
items.description: Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country on Friday, as haze from fires in neighbouring Indonesia again plunged local air quality to among the world’s worst. Toxic smoke from peatland as well as forest fires has shrouded towns and cities in the region for more than a month, sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing. The school closures came as Malaysia’s leader discussed the choking smoke with his Indonesian counterpart and called for an urgent regional meeting. Kuala Lumpur’s air quality worsened on Friday to hit a reading of around 224 on the index of Swiss-based monitor IQAir, which said that change pushed Malaysia’s capital past Singapore to be the “most polluted global major city”. Malaysia’s Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said she has instructed full school closures in four states and two federal territories as well as one partial closure in the central Pahang State. Schools were also closed on Friday in three districts in western Perak State. Malaysia’s education ministry could not immediately be reached for comment on whether schools will reopen on Monday. “In the future, we will ensure that any decision to close schools is notified in advance so that parents have sufficient time to prepare,” Fadhlina said late on Thursday. Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim weighed in on the matter on Thursday, saying schools should be closed as air quality readings reached 150 or higher on the Air Pollutant Index (API). “Appropriate measures must be taken by the relevant ministries and agencies to protect schoolchildren and students, including senior citizens and patients with respiratory illnesses,” King Sultan Ibrahim said. Under Malaysian guidelines, API readings above 100 are classified as unhealthy, above 200 as very unhealthy, above 300 as hazardous, while readings beyond 500 constitute the threshold for declaring a local emergency. ‘Necessary steps’ Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Thursday he discussed the fire situation with the Indonesian leader Prabowo Subianto. “The haze issue is indeed at a worrying level. And I have personally contacted President Prabowo,” Anwar said. “And he also agreed to take the necessary steps,” Anwar said, without going into specific details. He said Malaysia has been taking measures to combat the haze, including increasing attempts to trigger rain via cloud seeding. Indonesia’s government said “regular dialogue between the leaders is a natural part of the close relations” of the two nations. Experts said the flames are being fanned by a turbo-charged El Nino weather phenomenon , causing the worst pollution conditions in years. Anwar said he asked Malaysia’s Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to contact the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ secretariat for an urgent meeting between environmental ministers to discuss the matter. “So these are all the steps we are taking, but we are monitoring and will try the measures that we ought to take next,” Anwar said. Singapore’s air quality levels too dipped into the “very unhealthy” range with a reading of 209 on the AQI in Friday afternoon, according to the IQAir website. The AQI converts measurements of pollutants into a single figure indicating air quality and potential health risks. Readings above 150 are classified as unhealthy, while levels above 300 are considered hazardous.

items.title: Revue de presse de ce vendredi 9 octobre 2026
items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale de ce vendredi 9 octobre 2026 Al Bayane • Le Maroc a accueilli 15,7 millions de touristes à fin septembre 2026, en hausse de 5% par rapport à la même période de 2025, soit plus de 717.000 arrivées additionnelles, selon le ministère du Tourisme, de l'Artisanat et de l'Économie sociale et solidaire. Cette dynamique s'est renforcée en septembre, avec plus de 1,5 million de touristes accueillis, en progression de 8% par rapport à septembre 2025, précise le ministère dans un communiqué, notant que ces résultats confirment la solidité de la trajectoire de croissance du tourisme marocain et la capacité de la destination à maintenir sa dynamique au-delà des périodes de forte affluence. • La croissance des revenus de la cote est ressortie à +10,3% au premier semestre (S1) 2026 par rapport au S1-2025, affichant ainsi son niveau le plus élevé depuis S1-2022, selon Attijari Global Research (AGR). En effet, les revenus agrégés ont atteint 194,78 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) à fin juin 2026, contre 176,56 MMDH à fin juin 2025, indique AGR dans son récent « Research Report – Equity ». Al Ahdat Al Maghribia • Après les résultats enregistrés lors des précédentes opérations d’immatriculation foncière gratuite, le dispositif devrait être étendu en 2027 à 70 nouvelles zones rurales, contre 35 auparavant. Cette nouvelle opération devrait permettre à des milliers d’agriculteurs et de propriétaires ruraux de passer de la « propriété coutumière » à un titre foncier. Elle vise ainsi à renforcer la sécurité foncière tout en allégeant les charges financières liées à l’immatriculation pour les petits exploitants. • Le ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Ryad Mezzour, a indiqué que les conventions signées au cours des deux premiers jours de la 8e édition du Marrakech Airshow marquent l’émergence d’un « nouveau type » de partenariats, notamment dans le domaine de la défense. Il a notamment fait état d’un accord important portant sur le développement et la fabrication d’un drone marocain à partir d’une technologie nationale. S’exprimant en marge du salon organisé à Marrakech, Ryad Mezzour a également précisé qu’un accord avait été conclu pour l’acquisition de ce drone, estimant que cette démarche témoigne de l’existence d’un tissu national dans les industries militaire et aéronautique, intégré aussi bien sur le plan du développement que de la fabrication. Assahra almaghribia • Le Roi Mohammed VI préside, ce vendredi, l'ouverture de la première session de la première année législative de la 12e Législature. A cette occasion, le Souverain prononcera un discours devant les membres des deux Chambres du Parlement : la Chambre des Représentants et la Chambre des Conseillers, annonce le ministère de la Maison Royale, du Protocole et de la Chancellerie dans un communiqué. Le discours Royal sera retransmis en direct sur les ondes de la radio et à la télévision à partir de 15H45. • Le secteur de l’assurance au Maroc connaît une nouvelle phase de transformations réglementaires, économiques et technologiques. Celles-ci s’inscrivent dans une dynamique de restructuration des circuits de distribution des assurances, de révision des conditions d’accès à la profession d’intermédiaire en assurance et d’évolution de la tarification de l’assurance automobile, parallèlement à un élargissement de la couverture assurantielle à un plus grand nombre de citoyens et d’entreprises. Ces différents chantiers ont été au cœur des interventions des principaux responsables du secteur lors de la 10ᵉ édition de la rencontre annuelle de la Fédération nationale des agents et courtiers d’assurance au Maroc (FNACAM), organisée jeudi à Casablanca. items.title: LA 2028: Near misses and the crashouts, but Black Queens cannot afford another Olympic Games slip-up
items.description: For a country that prides itself as one of the best as far as women’s football on the African continent is concerned, Ghana never being at the Olympic Games is worrying. Since the introduction of women’s football at the Olympic Games in 1996, there have been seven more editions that have happened. However, in all of that, the Black Queens are yet to make an appearance. The closest Ghana has come to qualifying for the summer games was back in 2008, when they missed out on a spot to Brazil at the intercontinental playoffs. Just like their fate in the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), Ghana has enjoyed unsuccessful stints in their quest to win the coveted prize since the inception of the competition, losing three finals while they have had several semifinal appearances in between. It also relates to their dream of returning to the Women’s World Cup, even though, in that regard, they have been there on three occasions, the last being in 2007. Kim Lars Bjorkegren knows he can’t afford to disappoint once again after Ghana’s underwhelming performance at the 2026 WAFCON in Morocco two months ago, missing out on the final four before sealing a World Cup playoff spot. While the wait for a first appearance continues to prolong, here is a review of how Ghana has come close to reaching the Olympic Games in times past. Atlanta, Georgia, 1996 In the first edition, Ghana failed to make the needed stage required to qualify for the Olympics. This was after the Black Queens missed out on the qualification for the 1995 Women’s World Cup, which served as the qualifiers for the Olympic Games. Eventually, there was no African country present at the games in the United States of America. Sydney, Canberra and Melbourne 2000 Just like the 1996 edition, the top seven teams from the World Cup earned qualification to play at the Olympic Games in Australia. Once again, Ghana failed to qualify for the World Cup and eventually missed the opportunity to play at the Olympic Games again. Nigeria became the first African country to make the Olympics in that year. Athens 2004 Having seen the Black Meteors qualify for the Olympic Games in Greece, the Black Queens were hopeful of the same feat. With one slot allocated to Africa, there was a lot at stake. The Black Queens received a bye in the first round, then beat DR Congo on aggregate in the second round. However, they hit a snag in the third round. Ghana met Nigeria, and despite all of their great efforts, they fell short on penalties, with the Super Falcons going on to feature in back-to-back Olympic Games after beating South Africa in the final round. Beijing 2008 This is the closest the Black Queens came to sealing an Olympics slot. Their nemesis was Brazil. Ghana eased their way past Angola with a 4-1 aggregate victory in the first round. The second round gave Ghana a similar aggregate scoreline over DR Congo, making it to the final phase of the CAF qualifiers. With Ethiopia withdrawing, Ghana, Nigeria, and South Africa were played in a league format, with the Super Falcons taking the automatic spot. The Black Queens sealed second spot, which meant they had to play in the intercontinental playoff. The CONMEBOL-CAF playoff didn’t end well for the Black Queens, as they fell 5-1 to a Marta-inspired Brazil, bringing an end to their hopes of playing at the tournament in China. London 2012 Then came the challenge for the games in the United Kingdom, where Africa was guaranteed two slots. Ghana started its campaign in the second round, beating Guinea 7-1 on aggregate. However, the final round saw Ghana exit on the away goal rule. Cameroon and Zimbabwe went on to represent the African continent in that year. Rio 2016 In 2016, Ghana missed out on the plane to Brazil after losing to Cameroon on the away goal rule once again following a 3-3 aggregate score. This was after Ghana had been involved in the second round, where they beat Egypt 4-1 on aggregate to proceed to the third round of the qualifiers. Tokyo 2020 In the 2020 edition, Ghana featured in just two rounds. The Black Queens received a bye for the first round and made an entry in the second round of the qualifiers, facing Gabon. The team grabbed a 5-0 aggregate scoreline and advanced into the third phase of the qualifiers. After playing out a goalless draw at the Accra Sports Stadium in the first leg, the Black Queens lost 1-0 in Kasarani to Kenya. Paris 2024 The Black Queens started their campaign from the first round during the 2024 edition as they dispatched Guinea 7-0 on aggregate after the two games. They advanced to face Benin in the next round, which also saw them claim a 5-0 aggregate victory. Photo Credit: Seth Amoako Ghana then set up a clash with Zambia with a series of off-the-pitch issues leading to the first leg of the game at the Accra Sports Stadium. The Queens lost opening leg 1-0 but looked very certain to overturn the tie in Lusaka. However, there was heartbreak in Zambia when a lead was blown away in the dying minutes of the game after Jennifer Cudjoe picked up a red card with Ghana losing 4-3 on aggregate. The Queens have started the quest for Los Angeles in style with a 3-0 win over Mauritius in the first leg but they know they cannot take anything for granted from here.

items.title: Après la trêve internationale, les championnats européens de retour ce week-end
items.description: Après une longue période de trêve internationale, les championnats européens reprennent ce week-end avec comme affiche en Angleterre un choc Liverpool-Manchester City, tandis qu'en Liga le Real Madrid court déjà après les points pour ne pas être largué par Barcelone. Premier League : City dans le chaudron d'Anfield En pleine tempête après avoir été déclaré coupable de graves infractions financières, verdict dont le club a fait appel, Manchester City se déplace à Anfield dimanche lors de la 6e journée de Premier League. Leaders du championnat avec 5 victoires en autant de rencontres, les joueurs d'Enzo Maresca auront certainement le droit à un accueil bouillant de la part de Liverpool, 6e avec 9 points. Le champion en titre Arsenal, dauphin des Citizens avec 12 points, reçoit Leeds, invité surprise des places européennes (5e, 9 points), tandis que Brighton, qui occupe la troisième place du podium (10 points), se déplace sur la pelouse de Sunderland. La lanterne rouge Tottenham, avec deux points et aucun succès, se déplace chez un Manchester United encore pâle (12e). . Liga : le Real pour retrouver ses nerfs Alors que le Clasico face au Barça à la fin du mois approche, le Real Madrid peine toujours à retrouver un peu de sérénité. Déjà éloigné par son rival catalan (15 points contre 21), le club merengue, qui reste sur une défaite dans le derby madrilène, reçoit Villarreal (9e, 8 points). Avec ou sans Kylian Mbappé ? La star française, touchée à un genou avec les Bleus, a repris l'entraînement d'après les photos publiées par le club, mais a été l'objet d'énièmes critiques de la part de la presse espagnole et de supporters à propos de la gestion de sa blessure et de sa communication tapageuse dans sa campagne pour le Ballon d'Or. Solide leader de la Liga, le champion en titre barcelonais reçoit lui Getafe (11e), tandis que l'Atlético Madrid (2e, 16 points) se déplace chez le Deportivo Alavés (6e) et que le Betis Séville (3e, 16 points) accueille Osasuna (13e). . Bundesliga : Dortmund pour un sans-faute Leader avec 12 points, Dortmund ouvre la 5e journée de Bundesliga vendredi (20h30) dans son Westfalenstadion contre le Werder Brême, et espère poursuivre son sans-faute. Les hommes de Niko Kovac réalisent le meilleur début de saison du Borussia en Bundesliga depuis la saison 2015/16. La dernière fois que Dortmund a occupé le fauteuil de leader, c'était lors de la 33e et avant-dernière journée de la saison 2022/23, et l'avait cédé la journée suivante au Bayern, sacré champion in extremis à la 88e minute de la dernière journée. Avant de se rendre en Norvège à Stavanger pour affronter le Viking en Ligue des champions mardi (21h00), les Munichois (2e, 10 points) effectueront samedi (15h30) leur déplacement le plus court de la saison à Augsbourg. Derrière le Borussia et le Bayern, Fribourg (3e, 10 pts) recevra Schalke 04 dimanche (17h30) en clôture de la journée, alors que Leipzig recevra l'Eintracht Francfort samedi (18h30). . Serie A : l'Inter Milan peut prendre l'ascendant Pour la reprise de la Serie A, l'Inter Milan reçoit Parme samedi (18h00) dans le cadre de la 6e journée. En cas de victoire face à une équipe en crise (15e, 4 pts) qui a changé d'entraîneur lors de la fenêtre internationale, le champion d'Italie peut passer seul en tête, au moins provisoirement. Les deux autres co-leaders avec chacun 13 points, l'AS Rome et la Lazio, seront en piste dimanche: la Roma qui reste sur un nul 2-2 face à l'Inter, passe un nouveau test à Côme (8e, 10 pts), tandis que la Lazio reçoit le promu Monza (16e, 4 pts). Décevant 9e (7 pts) sous la conduite de Massimiliano Allegri, déjà sous pression, le Napoli pourrait récupérer son meneur écossais Scott McTominay, exploité du cœur le mois dernier, pour la réception samedi (20h45) du promu Frosinone qui pointe à une inattendue 6e place (10 pts). La Juventus Turin (7e, 10 pts) se rend dimanche chez l'autre surprise de ce début de saison Cagliari (4e, 12 pts). L'AC Milan (5e, 11 pts) rend de son côté visite à Sassuolo (10e, 7 pts). items.title: Wode Maya recounts how he won Miss Trudy’s heart with Shatta Wale’s song
items.description: Ghanaian YouTuber Wode Maya has recounted how his wife, Kenyan YouTuber Miss Trudy, believed in his dreams when he had nothing, and how he serenaded her with a Shatta Wale song. Speaking on Joy Prime’s Prime Time in an interview with host George Quaye, Wode Maya said he was honest with Miss Trudy from the very beginning about his situation. “When I met her, I told her like listen I don’t have anything right now but believe me we’re going to make it,” he said. According to him, because she believed in his dreams even when he had nothing to offer, he decided to compose songs for the two most important women in his life: his mother and Miss Trudy herself. “When she believed in my dreams, this was a song that like yeah, now that you believe in my dreams, I’m going to take bullet for you. So these are the two songs. So the first song was for my mom and the second one was for her,” he recounted. Wode Maya revealed that after he finally “bagged” Miss Trudy, he serenaded her with a hit song by Shatta Wale. He said he had just become hooked on Shatta Wale’s music at the time and was listening to Freedom every day, making it a special song in their relationship. “After that I just got into Shatta Wale so much. I started listening to Freedom like everyday. I loved it,” he said with a smile. The popular travel vlogger, who has built a huge following by documenting Africa for a global audience, said Miss Trudy’s belief in and support for him were key to his journey, which is why he continues to celebrate her.

items.title: Putin offers help to Iran to end Mideast war ahead of summit
items.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin vowed on Thursday to “do everything” to help end the Middle East war when he met Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian for talks ahead of a regional summit, Russian media reported. The leaders of two of the world’s most sanctioned nations met after arriving in Turkmenistan for a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) that starts on Friday in the Caspian Sea resort of Avaza. “We are ready to do everything that is in our power to contribute to the settlement of this situation,” said Putin. He added that Iran had made “real efforts to end the war” since US-Israeli attacks started on February 28, according to Russian news agencies. Putin also noted the “positive evolution” in Iran-Russia relations. The two countries have reinforced diplomatic and military links since Russia launched its offensive in Ukraine in February 2022, becoming increasingly reliant on each other. – Conflict impasse – Kyiv and Western countries have accused Iran of supplying Russia with Shahed drones and short-range missiles to pummel Ukraine. Russia has been accused of supplying data to Iran for its attacks on US targets in the Middle East. Putin and Pezeshkian also met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan last month. And in a call on Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian that he was ready to help mediate in the Middle East war, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported. The contacts came with Iran-US talks at an apparent impasse. Pezeshkian said this week that negotiations with Washington were “meaningless”. Diplomatic efforts to resolve Russia’s offensive in Ukraine also appear deadlocked, even as both sides intensify attacks. “We are engaged in dialogue, but every time we negotiate with the United States, they attack again,” Iranian state media quoted Pezeshkian as saying at the talks with Putin. Trump ruled out attacking Iran again before the US midterm elections on November 3, saying on Thursday that Washington was holding “productive discussions” with the Islamic republic. Pezeshkian said Tehran wanted to see a “final framework” to end the war. But he accused the United States of “trying to impose its policies and views on all countries”. “If the United States insists on pursuing a unilateral approach, a resolution will not be possible,” he said, according to state media. – Sphere of influence – Putin and Pezeshkian will attend the summit of the CIS — originally a grouping of former Soviet nations — with leaders of Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Turkmenistan and other Central Asia states. The Putin-Pezeshkian meeting was one of several bilateral encounters scheduled on the sidelines of the summit, according to Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov. The CIS was established in 1991 to ease the pain of the Soviet collapse and maintain ties among its former republics. Some states have left — Georgia withdrew following a 2008 war with Russia, Ukraine halted its participation after Moscow’s 2014 annexation of Crimea and Moldova left in 2023 as it sought closer ties with the European Union. For Russia, which has found itself isolated since launching the Ukraine conflict in 2022, the CIS proves that it “actually has the orbit and that it has its own sphere of influence that is fortified and institutionalised”, Temur Umarov, a researcher at the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center in Berlin, told AFP. But Friday’s meeting also comes at a time when several CIS members are seeking to diversify their economic and diplomatic partnerships, notably by strengthening ties with China and Western nations. “Even if Russia decides to use this platform to propagate anti-Western or anti-Ukrainian rhetoric, that does not mean the other members will automatically subscribe to its position,” Zhanibek Arynov, a Kazakhstan-based researcher specialising in Central Asian geopolitics, told AFP. items.title: Orange Guinée mise sur une dizaine d’influenceurs pour renforcer sa proximité avec le public
items.description: Orange Guinée renforce sa stratégie de communication digitale. L’opérateur de téléphonie a signé, ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026, à son siège de Koloma, des contrats avec neuf créateurs de contenus et influenceurs répartis en trois catégories : humour, lifestyle et show. Les nouveaux ambassadeurs auront également droit chacun un iPhone 18 Pro Max. Ils étaient 44 candidats au départ. Après une présélection ayant conduit à 13 profils retenus, neuf influenceurs ont finalement été choisis pour porter les messages de la marque Orange Guinée. La cérémonie de signature des contrats s’est déroulée en présence du directeur général de l’entreprise, Ousmane Boly Traoré, des cadres d'orange ainsi que des fans venus soutenir les influenceurs. Les nouveaux ambassadeurs qui signent désormais au côté de DjéliKaba Bintou, Saïfond, Kabakoudou et Serhou Guirassy, sont issus de trois univers de création de contenus. Dans la catégorie humour figurent Karim Kaba connu sous le nom Rimka ou Karim Djippö sur les réseaux sociaux, Diallo Piscine, Nga Nbalou. Le volet lifestyle regroupe Youyou, Crépin Lamah et El Yayus. Quant à la catégorie show, elle est représentée par Fresh DD, Tad et l’Afrique noire ainsi qu’IKK Show. À travers ce partenariat, Orange Guinée entend s’appuyer sur la notoriété de ces créateurs de contenus et leur capacité à mobiliser des communautés importantes sur les réseaux sociaux pour renforcer sa proximité avec les consommateurs. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le directeur général d’Orange Guinée, Ousmane Boly Traoré, a salué le travail des équipes marketing, qui lui ont permis de découvrir les profils retenus. Il a surtout insisté sur la nécessité de préserver la crédibilité des influenceurs auprès de leurs communautés. « Vous avez des millions de personnes qui vous suivent, que vous avez convaincues et qui ont certainement adhéré à votre discours. Aujourd’hui, qu’Orange Guinée vienne vers vous, c’est une marque de reconnaissance par rapport à votre propre travail », a-t-il déclaré. Pour ce resoonsqble, ce partenariat constitue également une responsabilité pour l’entreprise. Il a assuré que la marque devra veiller à ne pas compromettre la confiance dont bénéficient les créateurs de contenus auprès de leurs abonnés. « Nous ferons tout ce qu’il faut pour que cette acceptation d’être notre ambassadeur ne biaise pas votre crédibilité par rapport aux populations qui croient en vous et qui vous suivent », a-t-il ajouté, estimant qu’Orange Guinée devra être irréprochable aussi bien dans les messages véhiculés que dans les services proposés. Évoquant la durée de cette collaboration, Ousmane Boly Traoré a exprimé le souhait de voir cette union se prolonger bien au-delà de la durée des contrats, qu’il considère comme le début d’une relation appelée à s’inscrire dans le temps. Parmi les nouveaux ambassadeurs, Youssouf Baldé, connue sous le nom de Youyou, a exprimé sa satisfaction et présenté cette collaboration comme un message d’espoir pour la jeunesse guinéenne. « On peut naître, grandir et réussir en Guinée », a-t-elle affirmé, promettant de privilégier l’authenticité et la rigueur dans son travail avec l’opérateur. L’artiste comédien Thierno Saïdou Diallo, alias Diallo Piscine, a pour sa part qualifié cette nomination de chance et de responsabilité. Il s’est engagé à donner le meilleur de lui-même pour mériter la confiance d’Orange Guinée et de ses fans. À travers ce partenariat, l’opérateur entend s’appuyer sur la notoriété et la proximité de ces créateurs de contenu avec leurs abonnés pour renforcer sa communication digitale et son lien avec le public guinéen.

items.title: L'Arabie saoudite "exclut" une trêve avec les Houthis du Yémen
items.description: L'Arabie saoudite, dont la capitale Ryad connaît des attaques d'une ampleur inédite, notamment contre son aéroport, « exclut » dans l'immédiat une trêve avec les Houthis pro-iraniens du Yémen. Selon une source régionale qui s'est confiée vendredi à l'AFP, Ryad écarte tout « cessez-le-feu » tant que les forces gouvernementales yéménites, qu'elle soutient, n'auront pas récupéré les territoires dont se sont emparés récemment les Houthis. L'Arabie saoudite ne cèdera pas au « chantage militaire » des combattants houthis, a ajouté cette source sous couvert d'anonymat. D'autre part, l'autorité de l'aviation civile d'Arabie saoudite a annoncé vendredi la mort de trois Saoudiens dans les frappes réalisées jeudi sur l'aéroport de Ryad, qui ont été revendiqués par les combattants pro-iraniens houthis du Yémen. « Les attaques ont entraîné la mort de trois citoyens saoudiens » , a indiqué cet organisme, précisant que les frappes avaient visé des installations de l'aéroport ainsi qu'un avion de la compagnie nationale saoudienne. De son côté, la compagnie aérienne Saudia a indiqué qu'un de ses pilotes avait été tué et un de ses avions endommagés jeudi à l'aéroport de Ryad, contre lequel les combattants pro-iraniens houthis ont dit avoir mené une attaque. « C'est avec une profonde tristesse que Saudia annonce le décès du commandant de bord Hamoud Ali Alkalthami », a indiqué la compagnie nationale saoudienne dans un communiqué, évoquant un « incident » survenu à l'aéroport international du roi Khaled. The post L'Arabie saoudite "exclut" une trêve avec les Houthis du Yémen appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Why India's tens of millions of voter deletions have led to widespread protests
items.description: India’s verification exercise of its nearly one billion voters has sparked protests across the country, with opposition parties alleging that the removal of 130 million names from electoral rolls has unfairly benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s party. Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party are demanding the ouster of Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar and have vowed a huge protest ​in the capital, Delhi, on Saturday. Election Commission data cited by Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from ‌electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30m who could not be traced. The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions. They say the deletions have affected the outcome of some recent state elections that the BJP won, and have cast a shadow on the electoral process in the world’s biggest ​democracy. The BJP says Modi’s popularity and India’s economic growth are some reasons for their electoral dominance. Here are some details about the voter verification drive, which has become one of the biggest political controversies ​of Modi’s 12-year tenure ahead of crucial state elections starting early next year. What’s happening? Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party youth movement, farmers’ groups and opposition parties ⁠are set to protest in Delhi on Saturday, demanding the resignation of Kumar. Police say they have not granted permission, and CJP has reported preemptive detentions of some protest leaders. Sporadic protests have been going on across India ​since a report by the Indian Express newspaper in late September said Kumar’s two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems. The Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, ​and has denied favouring any party. Demonstrators take part in a protest organized by opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in Ahmedabad, India, on October 8. — Reuters Modi’s BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country’s democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Why does it matter? At least seven Indian states will hold elections next year, including BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh, the most populous and considered a bellwether state in national politics. Verification in Uttar Pradesh began in October 2025 and resulted in 13 per cent of names being deleted, according to local media reports. Voters with their names missing need to prove their credentials ​before being enrolled, and many have complained about the process. Verifying a billion voters: the controversy India started verification of its voter rolls last year ahead of elections in the eastern state of Bihar, ruled by a BJP ​coalition. The review has now covered the majority of Indian states. While voter roll revisions are routine, this round became controversial after large numbers of voters in states such as Bihar and West Bengal found their names missing from electoral ‌rolls and were ⁠unable to cast ballots. The BJP won power in West Bengal for the first time in May. Citing Election Commission data, the BJP says that of the 130m names deleted from voter lists, 28m are dead, 63m have relocated, 10m are duplicates and 30m could not be traced by officials. Opposition parties, including Congress, have accused Kumar of bias and alleged that the process benefits the BJP, charges the Election Commission and the party deny. The Indian Express story said the two deputies to the election commissioner had expressed concerns to Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, but those concerns were not taken into consideration. The Election Commission said all its decisions ​were lawful. The report prompted opposition leaders and members of ​the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, which in July forced ⁠the education minister to quit after weeks of protest, to launch nationwide demonstrations. Demonstrators break the barricade as they protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in Patna, India, on September 28, 2026. — Reuters What happens to voters removed from the rolls? The Election Commission says names are only removed when a voter has died, is mentioned more than once on the rolls, has moved to another region or is untraceable. Officers are required to record detailed reasons why a voter ​is deleted. People whose names do not appear in draft rolls can request inclusion before final voter lists are published and also raise appeals if such ​requests are denied. Voters excluded from ⁠final rolls can also challenge the decision. To participate in future elections, excluded voters must succeed in their appeals or apply for fresh registration. Opposition parties argue that arbitrary deletions and lengthy appeals prevented millions in Bihar and West Bengal from voting and could be used as a weapon in future elections. Election commission’s defence The Election Commission has defended itself from allegations of political bias, including at a rare press conference by Kumar last year, who asked the opposition to submit ⁠their allegations under ​oath. Kumar has had a difficult relationship with opposition parties since taking over as the election body chief in February 2025. Opposition ​lawmakers put forward a motion to have him removed earlier this year, but it was rejected by parliament. Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) attend a protest demanding women’s safety in Bengaluru, India, on October 8, 2026. — Reuters A 2023 law passed by Modi’s government grants the election commission chief immunity from prosecution for acts done in an official capacity. Amid the recent backlash, the Election Commission announced revisions ​to the verification process, including home visits by officials to collect documents and an extension of the deadline for final verification in some states.

items.title: ‘Where did you get dollars to save?’ Oshiomhole questions Obi over $150m claim
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Senator Adams Oshiomhole has challenged former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to explain how he accumulated $156 million in savings during his tenure, questioning how the funds were obtained when the Federal Government paid states’ allocations in naira. Oshiomhole, who represents Edo North in the Senate and is a former governor of Edo State, raised the questions during an interview with Symfoni TV published on Thursday. The former All Progressives Congress national chairman said he and Obi were members of the National Economic Council, chaired by the vice president, when governors sought to receive their federal allocations in dollars because of differences between official and market exchange rates. According to him, the Federal Government rejected the proposal, insisting that the naira was Nigeria’s recognised currency. “So all the allocations we receive are in naira. So I asked Obi, where did you get dollars to save? Did you receive naira from Abuja and go to bid for dollars to save for Anambra State?” Oshiomhole said. He insisted that the claim was untrue, adding that Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo had attempted to explain the financial issues surrounding Obi’s record. Oshiomhole described Soludo as an authority on financial matters, citing his background as an economist and his tenure as governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria. “If you know Soludo, I think you should accept that when it comes to financial questions, Soludo is the authority,” he said. The senator also challenged Obi’s claim that he did not borrow money while serving as governor, arguing that facilities obtained from the World Bank could constitute loans even when repayment was deferred. Oshiomhole said he also accessed World Bank facilities while serving as Edo governor, including funding instruments known as budget support. “They are loans. But he then went on to say that these are not loans you pay immediately. Because you are not paying it immediately, it’s not a loan?” he queried. “It’s in the books. And a future government will necessarily pay it anyway.” He argued that repayment moratoriums could allow an outgoing administration to leave office before its loans became due, leaving a successor government to meet the obligations. “Your tenure will have ended before the day you become mature for repayment,” Oshiomhole said, adding that this was what he believed Soludo had sought to explain about Obi’s financial record. The senator also disputed Obi’s account of an event organised by the Director General of the Debt Management Office (DMO) to recognise the former governor for allegedly not applying for loan approvals. Oshiomhole described the claim as “another lie”, although he did not provide further details in the excerpt of the interview to substantiate the allegation. Obi, who governed Anambra State from 2006 to 2014, has maintained that he did not leave the state burdened with debts. He reiterated his position during a recent interview on Arise Television while responding to allegations that his administration left outstanding loans and liabilities. However, Anambra State Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Law Mefor, had previously claimed that Obi left $123.77 million in debt at the end of his tenure. The latest comments have renewed debate over Obi’s financial record, particularly the distinction between accumulated savings, foreign currency holdings and outstanding loan obligations. Oshiomhole’s claims and questions come amid continued political exchanges over the management of public funds and the financial legacy of past administrations. items.title: Pilot among 3 Saudi nationals killed in attacks on Riyadh airport, authorities say
items.description: Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said on Friday that three Saudi nationals ​were killed and several people were injured in ‌two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday. In a statement on X, the General Authority of Civil Aviation said the ​first attack targeted airport facilities, while the second ​struck an aircraft belonging to Saudi state carrier Saudia. The ⁠injuries ranged from minor to severe, and the attacks ​caused material damage, it said, adding that airport operations had ​resumed and air traffic had returned to normal. Separately, the kingdom’s national carrier confirmed that a Saudia Airlines pilot was killed, and an aircraft was damaged at Riyadh airport. “It is with profound sadness that Saudia announces the passing of Captain Hamoud Ali Alkalthami,” the Saudi flag-carrier said in a statement, citing an “incident” at King Khalid International Airport. Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) also temporarily suspended its flight operations to Riyadh, citing the “situation in the Middle East”. PIA’s decision follows similar moves by several other airlines, including Lufthansa Group and three Indian carriers, which suspended flights to Riyadh on Thursday. A Lufthansa spokesperson told Reuters that the German group’s airlines would suspend flights to the Saudi capital until October 16, citing “current developments in the Middle East”. India’s largest airline, IndiGo, said it had cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh until Oct 9. Air India and Akasa Air also told Reuters that they had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital until October 10. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday they had attacked the airport with two cruise missiles. The group also ​said it had targeted an airport in the southwestern city ​of Najran, a claim Saudi authorities have not confirmed, and an airbase ‌in ⁠Khamis Mushait with ballistic missiles. The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen’s reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing ​an offensive by ​Yemen’s UN-recognised ⁠government to take back territory from the Houthis. The latest confirmed casualties come after Saudi authorities ​said on Wednesday that three people were killed in ​earlier ⁠strikes this week on Riyadh airport and Abha airport in the southwest of the country. A thick black column of smoke and flames rose from Riyadh airport in a video verified by Reuters . A witness and three people briefed on the matter said a stationary commercial plane had caught fire and caused the smoke, though the fire was later put out. After loud booms echoed across Riyadh on Thursday morning, several multinational firms in the King Abdullah Financial District told staff to work from home or evacuated employees, according to people familiar with the matter. Diplomats were instructed to shelter in place at their embassies, and at least one international school sent children into a basement for safety. The conflict, now an overspill of the ⁠US-Iran ​war, has stoked further upheaveal in ​a region already destabilised by the wider war, and threatens to draw other ​states into mountain fighting.

items.title: Le prix Nobel 2026 de la paix décerné à la Sud-Africaine Navanethem «Navi» Pillay
items.description: Le prix Nobel 2026 de la paix a été décerné à la Sud-Africaine Navanethem « Navi » Pillay, a annoncé le Comité Nobel vendredi 9 octobre, « pour ses efforts pour promouvoir la paix et le droit international ». Âgée de 85 ans, la juriste a notamment présidé la commission d'enquête indépendante de l'ONU qui a accusé Israël de commettre un génocide dans la bande de Gaza.

items.title: Pourquoi les élites russes ne se retournent-elles pas contre Poutine ?
items.description: Découvrez Le Grand Continent . Des idées et des analyses que l’on ne trouve nulle part. Mais que vous verrez bientôt partout. Dans votre boîte mail à partir de 8 euros par mois Le 21 février 2022, trois jours avant l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine, Vladimir Poutine avait convoqué une réunion élargie du Conseil de sécurité, retransmise à la télévision. Il s’agissait de décider s’il fallait reconnaître les deux « républiques » séparatistes de l’est de l’Ukraine, Donetsk et Louhansk. Plusieurs participants, estimant que la question était véritablement ouverte, ont appelé à la prudence. Sergueï Narychkine, le chef des services de renseignement extérieurs, a soutenu une proposition visant à accorder à l’Occident « une dernière chance » avant toute reconnaissance. Poutine l’a interrompu. Parlait-il de négociations ou de reconnaissance ? « — Je soutiendrais… — « Je soutiendrais » ou « je soutiens » ? — Je soutiens… — Alors, dites-le franchement : oui ou non ? » Visiblement ébranlé, Narychkine a finalement répondu « Oui » et, dans sa confusion, s’est prononcé en faveur du rattachement des républiques à la Russie plutôt que de leur indépendance. Poutine a laissé échapper un petit rire et l’a interrompu : « Veuillez vous asseoir. Merci. » Le public russe comme occidental a regardé cette scène et s’est posé la question évidente : pourquoi personne, dans cette salle, n’a empêché la guerre ? La question pourrait toutefois être mal posée, car l’élite russe avait cessé d’être une élite bien avant le début de la guerre. Pour comprendre pourquoi, il faut distinguer deux types de capacités d’action dont disposent ceux qui détiennent le pouvoir, et qui définissent une véritable élite. Comment l'élite russe a perdu ses deux pouvoirs Le premier pouvoir est stratégique. Il s’agit de la capacité d’influencer l’orientation de l’État, de faire évoluer une décision avant qu’elle ne soit prise, ou de lui opposer un argument auquel le dirigeant est au moins tenu de répondre. Le second est tactique : la capacité à manœuvrer dans le cadre d’une ligne de conduite déjà tracée, à retarder, à édulcorer, à réinterpréter, à protéger les siens ou à obtenir une contrepartie. La classe dirigeante russe a perdu le premier bien avant 2022, et, comme l’a montré la réunion du Conseil de sécurité, la guerre lui a fait perdre le second. Alexandra Prokopenko, « De souverains à serviteurs : comment la guerre contre l'Ukraine a redéfini l'élite russe », Hurst, octobre 2026. Poutine a consacré ses deux premiers mandats à démanteler toutes les tribunes à partir desquelles une élite pouvait s’exprimer politiquement. L’exemple le plus flagrant est celui des gouverneurs régionaux. En 2004, sous prétexte de lutter contre le terrorisme et au mépris d’une décision de la Cour constitutionnelle, le Kremlin a supprimé l’élection des gouverneurs au suffrage direct. Le Conseil de la Fédération, dont les gouverneurs eux-mêmes avaient été écartés peu de temps auparavant et qui était désormais composé de membres désignés par le Kremlin, a approuvé ce changement sans la moindre objection. En l’espace de quelques années, les désaccords entre les régions et le pouvoir central ont disparu, car les gouverneurs nommés ont cessé d’être des hommes politiques pour devenir des administrateurs dont les attributions se limitaient à l’économie régionale. Le monde des affaires a tiré la même leçon d’une série d’inspections menées par les services de sécurité et les autorités de régulation. L’ancien magnat des médias Vladimir Goussinski et l’oligarque Boris Berezovski ont tous deux quitté le pays au début des années 2000. L’affaire la plus retentissante a été la confiscation des biens et la condamnation à dix ans de prison de l’homme le plus riche de Russie, Mikhaïl Khodorkovski, propriétaire de la compagnie pétrolière Ioukos. Le message a été si bien reçu que, dans les années 2010, il n’était déjà plus nécessaire de le rappeler à qui que ce soit. La propriété restait soumise à la loyauté, et les conflits politiques avaient cédé la place à une rivalité bureaucratique pour attirer l’attention du dirigeant. L’annexion de la Crimée en 2014 a constitué un véritable test à grande échelle. Des centaines de fonctionnaires ont réorganisé les budgets, créé un ministère chargé des affaires et saisi des biens ukrainiens sans la moindre friction interne. Cinq mois après l’annexion officielle, un vice-Premier ministre (considéré comme libéral) a proposé à un ambassadeur européen une sélection de vins de Crimée. Le diplomate a refusé ; au sein de l’administration, cette proposition a été perçue comme une plaisanterie sans importance. En février 2022, les hauts responsables de l’économie russe savaient parfaitement pourquoi cette guerre n’avait aucun sens : des centaines de milliards de dollars de réserves placées dans les pays occidentaux, une forte dépendance technologique vis-à-vis des importations et une structure budgétaire fondée sur l’intégration aux marchés mondiaux. Sur ordre de Poutine, les banques et les plus grandes entreprises industrielles ont mené des tests de résistance afin d’évaluer la capacité de l’économie à faire face aux sanctions. Les résultats, selon lesquels une rupture avec l’Occident coûterait plus de 10 % du PIB, ont été transmis au président. Cependant, ces données n’ont jamais servi d’argument contre la guerre. L’espace dans lequel un tel débat aurait pu avoir lieu s’était en effet refermé des années auparavant. Ce que l’élite a su préserver jusqu’en 2022, c’est une capacité d’adaptation hors du commun. Privée du droit d’exprimer une opinion politique, elle a compensé en développant un art de la préservation : savoir qui appeler, quel poste au sein d’un conseil d’administration offre une protection, quand se taire et quand payer. Ses membres sont restés dans le système soit par crainte pour eux-mêmes, leurs proches et leurs équipes, soit par manque d’alternative, soit en raison de l’emprise de l’État et des services de sécurité sur leur carrière. La loyauté relève ici d’une stratégie de survie rationnelle, et non d’une adhésion aux ambitions de Poutine ni d’un soutien à sa personne. La guerre a bloqué toutes les issues Du côté de l’État, à l’été 2022, lorsque les entreprises ont commencé à rechigner à donner la priorité aux réparations et aux pièces détachées destinées à une « opération spéciale » qu’elles considéraient comme l’affaire des autres, la Douma a adopté une loi autorisant le gouvernement à contraindre n’importe quelle entreprise, quel que soit son régime de propriété, à accepter des commandes militaires de l’État et à réaffecter ses employés sans leur consentement. Le texte a franchi les trois lectures et les deux chambres en moins d’une semaine, et Poutine l’a promulgué sept jours seulement après son dépôt. Les entreprises n’ont même pas eu le temps de s’y opposer. « Tout pour le front », s’est emporté en privé le directeur d’une entreprise publique : « Mes équipes de réparation sont envoyées au ministère de la Défense, et ensuite on me passe un savon parce que je n’atteins pas les objectifs commerciaux. » En matière immobilière, le parquet a multiplié les actions en justice afin d’obtenir la restitution d’actifs à l’État, notamment des terrains à Barvikha, le village des datchas du Kremlin situé près de Moscou. La proximité avec les décideurs avait toujours fait office de talisman contre les prédateurs d’entreprises et les services de sécurité. Ce n’est plus le cas : « Que l’on penche d’un côté ou de l’autre, cela ne change plus rien », m’a confié un homme d’affaires classé parmi les vingt premières fortunes du classement Forbes. « Les documents de protection ne servent plus à rien. Avant, il suffisait de nommer un proche de Poutine au conseil d’administration pour être à l’abri. Aujourd’hui, même cela ne vous sauve plus. » Le message, résume-t-il, est clair : le « vieux capital » n’existe plus. Du côté de l’Occident, la porte de sortie s’est refermée. Les sanctions individuelles n’ont pas monté les capitalistes contre le Kremlin ; elles les ont même rendus plus vulnérables dans leur propre pays et plus dépendants du pouvoir. Le talent d’adaptation n’a pas disparu. La flotte fantôme, les niches laissées vacantes par les entreprises occidentales qui sont parties, le commerce florissant des intermédiaires — tout cela relève de l’initiative, mais d’une initiative qui s’inscrit dans la ligne imposée, sans jamais s’en écarter. Pourquoi les sanctions se sont-elles révélées inefficaces pour influencer l'élite russe ? Les sanctions n’ont pas placé les entreprises et l’élite russes devant le choix entre Moscou d’un côté, et Londres et le lac de Côme de l’autre. En substance, elles leur ont fermé ces deux destinations, c’est-à-dire l’Occident tout entier, et ne leur ont laissé que Moscou. Interdictions de visa, comptes bloqués, avoirs gelés, refus des banques, crainte des saisies : l’argent est rentré en Russie. Aujourd’hui, 97 % des dépôts des Russes fortunés sont concentrés dans des banques soumises à des sanctions, et cet argent alimente de facto l’économie de guerre. En effet, au bilan d’une banque, les dépôts ont pour contrepartie des crédits ; or, l’octroi de crédits reproduit pour l’essentiel le modèle à deux vitesses de l’économie russe. D’un côté, les marchés publics, liés pour l’essentiel à la guerre, bénéficient de crédits ; de l’autre, tout le reste stagne. Les personnes sanctionnées n’ont donc aucune issue : leur seule stratégie consiste à s’accrocher à ce qu’elles possèdent, c’est-à-dire à redoubler de loyauté. Sans ces sanctions individuelles, l’élite vivrait plus confortablement. Mais généralement, les sanctions ont surtout eu un autre effet : en désignant nommément les personnes, elles établissent leur complicité et leur ôtent l’alibi de n’être « que des hommes d’affaires » ou de simples exécutants qui « appuient sur des boutons ». Il est désormais possible d’identifier des personnes précises et les fonctions concrètes qu’elles exercent dans la chaîne de valeur militaire : achats, intermédiation financière, logistique, etc. Il n’en reste pas moins que ces sanctions punissent une position plutôt qu’un comportement. Or, aucun de ces mécanismes ne précise comment les personnes visées devraient se comporter pour que les sanctions soient levées ou assouplies. En d’autres termes, lorsque vous êtes inscrit sur une liste et que votre vie quotidienne est restreinte parce que vous siégez au conseil d’administration d’une entreprise publique, aucune mesure susceptible d’améliorer votre situation ne vous est proposée. Vous pouvez vous démener, transférer de l’argent en Ukraine, être poursuivi pour cela en Russie et finir en prison — vous, vos proches, vos collègues —, les sanctions resteront en vigueur : aucun texte ne prévoit leur levée si l’on condamne la guerre et finance l’Ukraine. Des sanctions sans issue constituent une condamnation, et non une incitation. Pour devenir incitative, la politique de sanctions doit donc offrir une alternative. Que peut faire l'Europe ? Premièrement, il ne faut pas rester les bras croisés à attendre une scission au sein de l’élite. Une élite qui a perdu ses deux formes de pouvoir ne proposera pas d’alternative, car elle a structurellement oublié comment s’y prendre. Ceux qui étaient prêts à partir par principe l’ont déjà fait ; ceux qui sont restés ont accusé les dissidents de naïveté ou de déloyauté, renforçant ainsi leur propre attachement au pouvoir. Deuxièmement, les sanctions individuelles ne constituent pas un moyen de pression sur Poutine, car les personnes visées n’en ont elles-mêmes aucun : « Pour mener un coup d’État, il faut être au palais. Nous n’y sommes pas », m’a confié l’un d’entre eux. Les sanctions ne font qu’accentuer leur dépendance vis-à-vis de Poutine. On peut les considérer comme une punition, mais pas comme un moyen de pression. Troisièmement, et c’est là que l’Europe entre en jeu, la solution réaliste n’est pas une révolution de palais. Mais après près de cinq ans de guerre, une fatigue écrasante s’est installée dans la société russe, tant au sein de la population que parmi les élites. La loyauté devient de plus en plus difficile à maintenir. Le désir d’en sortir est irrésistible ; mais il n’y a pas d’issue. L’équilibre dont jouissent des systèmes aussi fermés, qui semblent si stables de l’intérieur, ne peut être rompu que de l’extérieur. Un dialogue, et non une négociation, engagé non pas avec le Kremlin, mais avec ceux qui font réellement tourner l’État, à savoir les responsables économiques et les hommes d’affaires, pourrait donner à la classe dirigeante russe l’élan nécessaire pour reconquérir l’autonomie perdue. Ce soir-là, le 21 février 2022, Narychkine s’est vu demander de regagner sa place. Tous les participants à la réunion ont compris qu’on lui intimait de garder ses opinions pour lui et de ne pas prendre de risques. Près de cinq ans plus tard, rien, au sein du système, ne peut lui offrir l’occasion de se relever. C’est précisément pour cette raison que l’impulsion doit venir de l’extérieur. L’article Pourquoi les élites russes ne se retournent-elles pas contre Poutine ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .
