items.title: Government keeps appealing to striking teachers to resume work – Apaak
items.description: The government says it will keep engaging striking pre-tertiary teachers to return to the classroom as it works to resolve their grievances, with thousands of pupils affected by the industrial action. The teachers have been on strike for about two weeks over delayed promotion-related payments, a proposed allowance for teachers serving in deprived rural communities and the renewal of their collective agreement. The dispute has disrupted teaching and learning, prompting renewed calls for an early resolution. The Deputy Minister of Education, Dr Clement Apaak, said the government was committed to addressing the concerns and did not regard the teachers as adversaries. He maintained that appealing to them to resume work was part of efforts to minimise the impact of the strike while negotiations continued. “It’s not a crime to plead. So as long as they are not in the classroom, we will continue to plead with them,” Dr Apaak told Citi FM on Thursday, October 8, 2026. He added: “We are not antagonistic. We are not challenging their demands. We have not said anywhere that they are not justified.” Dr Apaak said the government was particularly concerned about the interruption to pupils’ education and would continue to appeal to teachers to return to their classrooms while their concerns were addressed. “We will continue to supplicate. We are lying down prostrate. We are on our knees pleading with our teachers to come back to the classroom whilst we address their legitimate concerns,” he said. He declined to discuss the specific areas of disagreement in the negotiations, explaining that it would be inappropriate to disclose details while discussions were still underway. He, however, expressed hope that progress would be made, including on the processing of outstanding promotion-related payments for affected teachers.

items.title: Dr Daniel Acquaye urges Christian business leaders to build sustainable enterprises
items.description: Agribusiness expert and Chief Executive Officer of Agri-Impact Ltd, Dr. (h.c.) Daniel Fahene Acquaye, has urged Christian business leaders and entrepreneurs to prioritise business sustainability, succession planning and strategic investment to build enterprises that can thrive across generations. Dr Acquaye, who also serves as Chairman of the Apostolic Professionals Network (APN), made the call at the maiden Apostolic Business Leadership Summit, organised by the network on Thursday, October 8, 2026, at the Headquarters of The Apostolic Church- Ghana in Accra. He said the high rate of business failures in Ghana and across Africa underscores the need for entrepreneurs to establish strong systems and structures that protect their investments and ensure continuity beyond the lifetime of their founders. Dr Acquaye expressed concern that many businesses in Ghana collapse before their founders have the opportunity to pass them on to the next generation, unlike enterprises in some developed economies that have survived for several generations. “There’s a growing concern among businesses, especially in Ghana and Africa. When you go to Europe and meet an enterprise, the first thing they would say is, ‘This is a family business, and we are the third generation or the fourth generation.’ They have been able to pass on their businesses from one generation to the other,” he said. “Now, when you come to our setting, the first generation will not even expire, but the business will expire.” Dr Acquaye attributed business failures to several factors, including the absence of effective succession plans, weak organisational structures, inadequate financial management and the inability of businesses to withstand changes in leadership. He noted that some enterprises collapse when their founders become incapacitated or die, while others struggle to survive because they lack the systems required to protect their resources and reinvest profits for growth. “We can’t continue to have businesses like that,” he stressed. He urged business owners to institutionalise their operations, safeguard their investments and develop succession strategies that would enable their enterprises to grow beyond their founders. Plan for retirement Dr Acquaye also cautioned against waiting until retirement to venture into business, particularly in the agricultural sector, describing it as a potentially risky approach to investment. He encouraged prospective entrepreneurs to develop their business ideas early, acquire the necessary experience and understand the risks involved before committing their retirement savings. Business leadership is a divine calling The President of The Apostolic Church-Ghana, Apostle Dr Aaron Ami-Narh, urged Christian business leaders to see their enterprises and leadership positions as a calling from God, with a responsibility to influence society and advance His purposes. Drawing lessons from the biblical account of Queen Esther, he challenged participants to reflect on why they had been given their talents, opportunities and positions of influence. “Your business is not just a business; it’s your calling. Your leadership role is not just a role; it is your calling and your mandate, and God is using it for something,” he said. Apostle Ami-Narh noted that Christian professionals and entrepreneurs had a responsibility to use their positions to make a difference rather than approach their work solely as a means of earning a living. Preventing revenue leakages Also addressing the gathering, Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), Elder Professor Samuel Antwi, called on business owners to take deliberate steps to prevent revenue leakages and improve operational efficiency. He emphasised the need for strong internal controls, effective procurement practices and the recruitment of employees with integrity to protect business resources and promote sustainable growth. “Put in processes to prevent, detect and correct fraud. Watch who you employ into your business. They can make or unmake your business. If I catch you stealing, you are out,” he said. “Look for men and women with integrity and employ them. It solves half of your leakage problem,” he added. The maiden Apostolic Business Leadership Summit was held under the theme, “Equipping Christian Business Leaders for a New Era” and brought together business leaders, professionals, entrepreneurs and industry experts. The Apostolic Professionals Network is a professional body within The Apostolic Church-Ghana established to raise and prepare a pool of professional men and women who can contribute to the professional development of the Church. The Network also seeks to nurture and empower young entrepreneurs by creating platforms for effective networking among professionals and business communities. Through training, motivation and mentorship, APN aims to support aspiring professionals while promoting Christian values, ethics and Godly maturity in members’ professional and business relationships. The maiden Apostolic Business Leadership Summit forms part of APN’s efforts to equip Christian professionals and entrepreneurs with the knowledge, skills and networks needed to thrive in an evolving business environment. Other seasoned speakers and industry experts who spoke at the summit include Deputy CEO of Agri-Impact Ltd, Mrs. Juliana Asante-Dartey, General Manager of JP Petroleum, Mr Joshua Larbi; Risk and Compliance Officer at Mobile Money Fintech Ltd, Mr Godwin Tamakloe; Partner at PwC Ghana, Mr Hayfron Aboagye, Managing Partner at Newage Agric Solutions Limited, Roland Quaye, Chief Farmer at Agokings, Nana Owusu-Achau among others.

items.title: Chief Justice urges employers to tackle mental health stigma in workplaces
items.description: Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has called on employers and public institutions to establish supportive workplace environments where people experiencing mental health challenges can seek help without fear of stigma, discrimination or exclusion. He said mental well-being must be treated as an essential part of a healthy and effective workplace, urging institutions to introduce policies that prioritise staff welfare and make professional mental healthcare more accessible. The Chief Justice made the appeal in a speech read on his behalf by Supreme Court Judge Justice Sophia Rosetta Bernasko-Essah at the 2026 World Mental Health Day celebration at the Court Complex in Accra. The event, organised by the Greater Accra Regional Health Service and the Judicial Service of Ghana, was held on the theme, “Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change.” Justice Baffoe-Bonnie said mental health discussions must move beyond statistics and diagnoses to recognise the lived experiences of affected people. He noted that fear of judgement and exclusion often prevents individuals from speaking openly about their struggles. “We must listen with empathy, most importantly, we must let those experiences inform how we design policies, provide support, and respond to people going through difficult periods in their lives,” he said. He observed that staff of the Judicial Service operate in a demanding environment, often dealing with conflict, trauma, loss, crime and family disputes, which can affect their mental well-being. He stressed that seeking help should not be regarded as a sign of weakness. The Chief Justice said the well-being of judicial officers and staff was vital to an effective justice system, adding that screening for chronic medical conditions and mental health assessments could promote prevention, early detection and timely intervention. “As a society we must move from merely sympathising with people experiencing mental health challenges to creating systems of support,” he said, urging employers to sustain conversations on mental health, encourage colleagues to support one another and promote professional help-seeking.

items.title: 52,000 teachers’ promotion payments targeted for October 15
items.description: Teachers whose promotions have been delayed could begin receiving their salary adjustments and arrears by October 15, as the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department works to clear the records of 52,000 affected staff. The payment process is now at the verification stage, following the submission of promotion input forms and letters by the Ghana Education Service (GES). Officials are checking the documents to establish which teachers’ records meet the requirements for validation and payment. Controller and Accountant-General Kwasi Agyei said the department had received all the required forms for the 52,000 teachers as of 2 p.m. on Thursday, October 8. He indicated that records not cleared during the current payroll exercise would be handled through a supplementary payroll and reflected in the affected teachers’ salaries later. “We are verifying them, and whatever is verified and validated, as the Deputy Minister said, the intention is to pay on the 15th or before the 16th of October,” Mr Agyei told Citi FM on Thursday, October 8. He said the validation exercise was expected to be completed by next week. The exercise follows a September 28 directive from Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu requiring the GES Director-General to submit details of all promoted teachers to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to facilitate the payment of outstanding salaries and arrears. The delayed payments have been among the grievances raised by the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG). The unions have embarked on industrial action over promotion delays, conditions of service and deprived-area allowances, among other outstanding concerns.

items.title: Nzema chiefs honour Lands Minister, demand sustainable revival of Adamus Resources
items.description: The Paramount Chief of the Eastern Nzema Traditional Area, Awulae Blay IX, has led a delegation of chiefs and Queen Mothers to honour the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, while urging the government to ensure that the planned revival of Adamus Resources Limited delivers jobs, investment and lasting economic benefits to the Nzema area. The delegation, comprising sub-chiefs and Queen Mothers, conferred a developmental chieftaincy title on Mr Buah in recognition of his contribution to Ellembelle and the wider Nzema area. Awulae Blay IX also commended the Minister for his efforts to sustain the legacy of Ghana’s first President, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, particularly through the annual Nkrumafest celebration. A traditional stool was presented to the Minister to symbolise the honour. The chiefs used the courtesy call to urge the Ministry to closely monitor the government’s 12-month roadmap for Adamus Resources, stressing that the mine’s revival should translate into jobs, improved livelihoods and investment opportunities for local communities. They also petitioned President John Dramani Mahama, through the Minister, to consider renaming Ghana Gas as “Atuabo Gas” to strengthen the sense of local ownership of the facility. Responding, Mr Buah thanked the traditional authorities for the honour and reaffirmed his commitment to the development of Nzema and the Western Region. He said the committee established by the President to oversee Adamus Resources had been tasked with ensuring that the company settles its outstanding liabilities, develops a sustainable revival plan and attracts fresh capital, including through potential equity participation by additional partners. The Minister said Adamus Resources would engage the traditional authorities to hear their concerns and incorporate them into the revival process, with the ultimate aim of ensuring sustainable operations and tangible benefits for the people of Nzema. He also assured the delegation that government would continue to address development needs in the area, including roads and other critical infrastructure.

items.title: ExxonMobil return talks emerge as GIPA CEO holds back details
items.description: Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) CEO Simon Madjie says there have been talks about ExxonMobil returning to Ghana. But he declined to disclose details, leaving further comment to the energy authorities. “I knew that there were some talks for them to come back. It’s not something that can be disclosed now.” Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Madjie referred questions about the discussions to the Minister of Energy and the Petroleum Commission. “So I, I think you leave that entirely to the Minister of Energy and Petroleum Commission.” His remarks offered a limited indication of discussions about a possible return. He gave no timeline or terms. He also did not say how far the talks had progressed. The issue arose when the host asked about multinational companies seeking to enter or return to Ghana’s petroleum sector. The host recalled earlier comments from the Energy Minister about companies such as Shell and ExxonMobil. Mr Madjie initially outlined other developments in the sector. He said the Petroleum Commission and the ministry would have much of the detail. “But what we all know is that from the Africa Oil Week, Chevron and Shell signed an MOU to look at work in the Eastern Keta Basin. So that’s ongoing.” He also cited reported interest from Petrobras in examining some of Ghana’s petroleum acreages and blocks. Alongside that interest, Mr Madjie pointed to investment announcements by companies already operating in the country. He cited plans by the Jubilee partners to invest $2 billion and drill 20 wells in the Jubilee field. He also referred to a $1.5 billion announcement by ENI and its partners. “And so there’s a lot of activities within that space. I’m sure folks at the Petroleum Commission will give you a lot more technical details.” But when the host returned specifically to ExxonMobil, Mr Madjie held back. His response acknowledged talks about a return without confirming an agreement or a decision by the company to resume operations.

items.title: Council of State meets teacher unions over strike today
items.description: The Council of State is set to engage teacher unions on Friday, October 9, as efforts intensify to resolve the industrial action by pre-tertiary teachers over outstanding employment-related concerns. The meeting, scheduled for 1:00 p.m. at the Council’s Secretariat, will bring together representatives of the unions and Council members to discuss issues including delayed promotions, deprived-area allowances and negotiations on a Collective Bargaining Agreement with the Ministry of Education. An invitation signed on behalf of the Chairman of the Council’s Economic and Social Development Committee, HRM Drolor Rosso Adamtey I, said the engagement would allow the unions to present their concerns to the Council. The National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) have cited these outstanding matters among the reasons for their industrial action. Meanwhile, Controller and Accountant-General Kwasi Agyei says his department has processed the promotion records of 52,000 teachers and received the required input forms from the Ghana Education Service (GES). He said the update was as of 2 p.m. on Thursday, October 8, paving the way for the necessary verification ahead of salary adjustments and payment of arrears. The processing follows a September 28 directive by Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu asking the GES Director-General to submit the relevant data to facilitate payments. Friday’s meeting is expected to provide a platform for discussions on the remaining concerns as stakeholders seek a resolution to the dispute.

items.title: Ntim Fordjour appeals to Mahama to abandon regulation restricting preaching in buses
items.description: Senior Pastor of Victory Bible Church International’s Higher Heights Sanctuary in East Legon and Assin South MP, Rev. John Ntim Fordjour, has appealed to President John Dramani Mahama to intervene over regulations restricting preaching in moving commercial vehicles, arguing that the measure could expose pastors and evangelists to imprisonment for sharing their faith. The Ranking Member of Parliament for the Defence and Interior Committee said he had been preaching on commercial buses since around 2007, when he began evangelising in Tarkwa. He questioned why the practice was now being treated as a nuisance and called on the President to direct that the regulation be abandoned. I begun evangelizing and preaching freely in commercial buses in Tarkwa around 2007. Now they want to ban preaching in buses. I risk going to jail if I continue preaching JESUS in buses. But what shall separate me from the love of God? Shall persecution or senseless laws stop us from preaching the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ freely everywhere? Mr President, please order them to abandon this bogus regulation which seeks to jail innocent Pastors and Evangelists – simply for preaching in buses. Now preaching JESUS in buses is described as NUISANCE? Or this is also part of the unpopular policies your Ministers are pushing without your approval? Who is really in charge in this govt? We will continue to PREACH JESUS in buses, on the street, on campuses, in markets and wherever we shall find souls. We will be undeterred by these anti-preaching regulations. Thank God for the inspiration for this book which occupied my passion a few years ago -PREACHING JESUS. — John Ntim Fordjour MP (@NtimFordjour) October 8, 2026 “Mr President, please order them to abandon this bogus regulation which seeks to jail innocent Pastors and Evangelists – simply for preaching in buses,” he wrote in a social media post. Rev. Ntim Fordjour also questioned whether the policy reflected President Mahama’s position or was being advanced by some ministers without his approval. “Or is this also part of the unpopular policies your Ministers are pushing without your approval? Who is really in charge in this govt?” he asked. His appeal follows the enforcement of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519), which prohibit preaching and hawking on public service vehicles while in motion. The regulations prescribe a fine of between 10 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both for offenders. He maintained that he would continue preaching in public spaces despite the restrictions.

items.title: Volta youth farmers commend Agric Minister, appeal for markets for cassava growers
items.description: The Volta Youth in Agriculture has congratulated the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Mr Eric Opoku, on his dedicated leadership and efforts to advance agricultural production. The youth group, however, appealed for markets for young cassava farmers in the region. Madam Joy Fiamawle, the Public Relations Officer of the group, in an interview, commended the Minister for his commitment to make agriculture more productive, resilient and attractive to the youth in general. “The Minister’s emphasis on increasing food production, supporting farmers, promoting agricultural value chains and building the capacity of young people to take part meaningfully in the sector is an important step towards a stronger and more sustainable agricultural economy,” she said. Madam Fiamawle described agriculture as more than an economic activity, and called it a powerful vehicle for job creation, youth empowerment, food security, poverty reduction and national development. She explained that the group appreciated initiatives and policies that placed farmers and young agricultural entrepreneurs at the centre of Ghana’s development agenda. She said: As a group, we also welcome the Minister’s efforts to improve access to agricultural inputs, irrigation, mechanisation, markets, technology, and other resources needed to raise productivity. “We believe that, with the right support, young people can become the next generation of commercial farmers, agribusiness owners, processors, exporters and agricultural innovators.” She encouraged the Ministry to keep prioritising youth-led agriculture, particularly in regions such as the Volta, which the group said has significant potential for crop production, livestock, aquaculture, agro-processing, and agribusiness. According to the group, a deliberate national programme that gives young farmers access to land, affordable financing, irrigation, improved seeds, mechanisation, extension services, storage and processing facilities, and guaranteed markets would significantly accelerate the transformation of the sector. The group further suggested that stronger links between farmers and institutional buyers, including schools, hospitals, hotels, restaurants, and food processors, could create sustainable markets for locally produced commodities. The group raised a specific concern about young cassava producers, adding that “many are becoming discouraged because they cannot find buyers for what they grow. We demand initiatives to secure markets for them.” The Volta Youth in Agriculture assured the Minister of its willingness to work with the government and other stakeholders to promote agriculture among the youth, and pledged to continue to champion the message that agriculture is a business, a source of employment, and a pathway to prosperity. The group said it was confident that with sustained leadership, collaboration and investment, the country could reduce its dependence on imported food, increase domestic production and build a competitive agricultural sector that could feed the nation and create wealth. They said that the future of agriculture in the country would be brighter and that the youth must be at its heart.

items.title: Mahama commissions expanded production line at Nestlé Ghana Ltd
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday commissioned the expanded evaporated milk production line at Nestlé Ghana Limited in the industrial city of Tema. President Mahama said Tema was a city where Ghana’s founding President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, planted the industrial ambitions of a young republic, and it remains the place where that ambition was most visibly at work. The President noted that investment that was being commissioned retired a production line that served the factory faithfully for more than 30 years but had reached the limits of its capacity. It is being replaced with an expanded factory production line capable of producing nearly 30,000 tons per year. Using the newly commissioned line, President Mahama explained the government’s flagship 24-Hour Economy programme to mean “a factory that never sleeps, it works 24-7, and it supports approximately 1,200 full-time workers and about another 1,300 third-party workers.” The President said he was happy to announce that 94.4 per cent of the employees of Nestlé were Ghanaian, saying, “this figure is most important because it shows whether a company is creating opportunities for Ghanaians as it grows its business, and to its credit, Nestlé has done that.” “Kwame Nkrumah planned Tema as Ghana’s industrial city, and I am pleased to say that Tema is regaining its glory days. The Port of Tema has expanded. Tema Oil Refinery is back, at work again. We are working on reviving VALCO,” he said. President Mahama said the Arise Industrial Enclave was progressing, and many industries like Nestlé existing in the Tema enclave were expanding their production. This, he said, was because the investment climate was good; adding that foreign direct investment had risen from 624 million Ghana cedis in 2024 to 2.62 billion dollars in 2025. “Interest rates are falling, with spreads between nine per cent and 13 per cent. Inflation, which stood at 23.8 per cent, is down to about 5.2 per cent, and our long-suffering local currency, the cedi, has regained its strength and is relatively performing very well,” he said. To the management and staff of Nestlé Ghana Limited, President Mahama said the plant was a monument to what partnership, purpose and patriotism could achieve together. “You belong to an institution with a proud heritage in this country and the courage to continue investing in this country’s future,” he said. “So, keep pushing the frontiers of growth, deepen your bonds with Ghanaian farmers and suppliers, and keep creating opportunities for young people and for this nation, Ghana,” he urged. President Mahama commended the Nestle Ghana Ltd for supporting the President’s Independence Day Award for schoolchildren for almost 30 years. He called for continual partnership with the government as the nation and Nestle both prepared to celebrate their 70th anniversary, saying, “let today be our shared dedication, our shared declaration to the world: we are not finished, we are only starting”. Madam Salomé Azevedo, the Managing Director of Nestlé Ghana Ltd, said the milestone the company had achieved reflected its commitment to local production and their confidence in Ghana’s very bright future.

items.title: Chief of Staff urges journalists to uphold accuracy, fairness
items.description: The Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has urged journalists to uphold accuracy, fairness and professional ethics while using their platforms to hold public officials accountable. He said journalists must verify information before publication, distinguish facts from allegations, respect privacy and human dignity, declare conflicts of interest and openly correct errors. Mr Debrah made the call in Accra on Wednesday when he launched the 30 th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards and inaugurated a nine-member awards committee. He said the media had a critical role in Ghana’s democracy and urged practitioners not to allow “the race to publish first” to compromise national peace or individuals’ rights and reputation. “We may disagree with a headline or a conclusion, but disagreement is not hostility, and scrutiny is not disloyalty,” he said. Mr Debrah said the rise of digital media had expanded opportunities for journalism and enabled young people to create and disseminate content without necessarily working from traditional newsrooms. He, therefore, called on the GJA to deepen training, mentorship and engagement with digital content creators to ensure that innovation and professional ethics advanced together. The Chief of Staff urged the awards committee, chaired by Mr Kobby Asmah, former Editor of the Graphic Communications Group, and member of the National Media Commission, to work with fairness, independence and clear standards in selecting award winners. He said the awards should recognise journalism that was accurate, courageous, original, innovative, and useful to the public. Mr Felix Kwakye Ofosu, the Minister in charge of Government Communications, said the Government was committed to protecting journalists and deepening the frontiers of free speech. He condemned the recent alleged assault of journalists during a demolition exercise at the La Pleasure Beach and said the Government would pursue the matter to its logical conclusion. Osahen Alexander Afenyo-Markin, Minority Leader of Parliament, also urged journalists to strengthen investigative reporting and pursue issues of public interest. He said the media had a greater responsibility to seek answers when parliamentary oversight was constrained, urging journalists to “maintain absolute focus on the facts” and demand accountability. Mr Albert Kwabena Dwumfour, GJA President, said the awards were intended to recognise journalism that informed public debate, held power to account, exposed wrongdoing and contributed to national development. He expressed concern about recent attacks on journalists allegedly by personnel of the Ghana Armed Forces, and demanded action on the matter within two weeks. The 30 th GJA Media Awards will be held on November 7, 2026, in Accra, with President John Dramani Mahama as the Special Guest of Honour and keynote speaker. The Speaker of Parliament and Chief Justice are also expected to attend. The GJA said it received 327 entries from 206 journalists for this year’s awards.

items.title: Mahama pays a working visit to Three Dreamer Manufacturing
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday paid a working visit to Three Dreamer Manufacturing Company in the industrial and port city of Tema in the Greater Accra Region. The Company is into the manufacturing and distribution of fast-moving consumer goods such as diapers, sanitary pads, toilet rolls, non-dairy creamer, biscuits, candies, fish snacks (aborbi), beef snacks, LED bulbs and tin foods. President Mahama in his address thanked the Management and workers of the factory for their contribution to Ghana’s industrial development. He encouraged them to continue working hard, continue producing for Ghana and continue looking beyond Ghana to the opportunities available across the African market. He said in the run-up to the 2024 elections, the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC) in its manifesto promised the implementation of the 24-Hour Economy. The President said Three Dreamer Manufacturing Company was a testimony to one of the practical ways in which that policy was beginning to translate into opportunities for their people. He said the 24-Hour Economy was not only about establishing new factories but also about supporting existing factories to expand their operations, increase production and employ more people. He said already, existing factories were employing more people because of the opportunities being created through the 24-Hour Economy Market. “If this factory was not here today, many of the young people we see working here would probably be at home without jobs,” he said. He added: “This is why we must continue to support local manufacturing and create opportunities for our young people.” President Mahama said they had the capacity to produce many of the things they consume locally; declaring that they were not only producing for the Ghanaian market and that they could also produce for export. “Look at the tin tomatoes and light bulbs being produced here. These are products that we can manufacture locally and export to other African markets,” the President said. He reiterated that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) provides them with a huge opportunity to expand their production and access markets across the continent. He said when they produce locally and export to other African countries, they create jobs for their people, generate income for businesses and strengthen their economy. “I am particularly happy to see the enthusiasm among the young people working here. I admire how happy you are because you now have employment and an opportunity to earn a living,” President Mahama said. He further encouraged the staff to support their employers; saying “assist your bosses to make more income so that they can expand their businesses and employ even more people”. He said the success of a factory depends not only on the owners and management, but that the workers also had an important role to play through hard work, discipline and commitment. President Mahama said when the business grows, the workers also benefit because the company would be able to create more opportunities and employ more people. He said they had earlier visited Nestlé Ghana Limited, where they also witnessed the expansion of production lines and that these developments show that existing companies were responding to the opportunities in the nation’s economy by increasing their production capacity. President Mahama said their responsibility as Government was to continue creating the right environment for businesses to produce, expand and employ more people, promising that the government would continue to pursue policies that strengthened the Ghanaian cedi and create a stable environment. “We have seen inflation come down, and we are working to ensure that the stability of the economy is sustained. A stronger and more stable economy will provide businesses with greater confidence to invest, expand their operations and create jobs,” the President said.

items.title: Shell, Chevron sign exploration MoU as Petrobras eyes Ghana’s oil blocks
items.description: Shell and Chevron have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore opportunities in Ghana’s Eastern Keta Basin, Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) CEO Simon Madjie has said. Brazil’s Petrobras has also expressed interest in the country’s oil acreage and blocks, adding to activity in the petroleum sector. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Madjie said work involving Shell and Chevron was ongoing. “But what we all know is that at Africa Oil Week, Chevron and Shell signed an MOU to look at work in the Eastern Keta Basin. So that’s ongoing.” He pointed to Petrobras’s reported interest as another development in the sector. “We also saw the interest of Petrobras announced in the newspapers, you know, to really look at some of the acreages and blocks that the country has”. Mr Madjie placed these developments alongside major investment announcements by companies already operating in Ghana’s oil industry. He cited plans by the Jubilee partners to invest $2 billion and drill 20 wells in the Jubilee field. He also highlighted a $1.5 billion announcement by ENI and its partners. “And so there’s a lot of activities within that space. I’m sure folks at the Petroleum Commission will give you a lot more technical details.” His comments outlined both interest in Ghana’s oil blocks and investment plans involving existing operations. However, he deferred questions about the technical details to the Petroleum Commission and the ministry. Asked specifically about a possible return by ExxonMobil, Mr Madjie acknowledged that talks had taken place. He declined to disclose further information. “I knew that there were some talks for them to come back. It’s not something that can be disclosed now.” He directed further questions on ExxonMobil to the authorities overseeing the sector. “So I, I think you leave that entirely to the Minister of Energy and Petroleum Commission.”

items.title: Mahama urges Ghanaian businesses to build beyond founders
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has urged Ghanaian entrepreneurs to build businesses that can survive beyond their founders, describing succession planning as critical to the long-term sustainability of indigenous enterprises. President Mahama said the collapse or decline of many Ghanaian-owned businesses after their founders retired or died remained a challenge to the development of a strong local private sector. He made this known during a visit to Kasapreko Limited as part of a tour of selected companies, including Nestle Ghana Limited, Three Dreamers Manufacturing, and Kasapreko Limited, where he commended the company for its growth, expansion and increasing presence in international markets. He cited Kasapreko Company Limited as a model of a Ghanaian enterprise that had successfully positioned itself for continuity, despite the retirement of its founder. He said the company’s ability to transition leadership to the next generation while continuing to expand its operations demonstrated the importance of building institutions rather than businesses that depended solely on their founders. “Kasapreko is also a model for Ghanaian enterprise. Often, when the founder of a business either retires or passes away, the business collapses,” he said. President Mahama congratulated Kasapreko Company Limited on its successful listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange, saying the company’s experience demonstrated that listing did not necessarily mean losing control of a business. He noted that Kasapreko had raised GHS 700 million through the listing, which was being invested in the company’s new factory at Adiamso, and expressed confidence that the expansion would lead to the establishment of more factories and create additional employment opportunities for Ghana’s youth. He said it gladdens his heart when he visits factories like that, stressing that “This is what it’s all about: creating jobs for our young people.” President Mahama urged Ghanaian business owners to deliberately create structures and systems that would enable their enterprises to remain productive and competitive after the founders had exited, saying that such continuity was important if Ghana was to develop strong indigenous companies capable of creating jobs, generating wealth and contributing significantly to national development. He said Kasapreko’s transformation from a relatively small Ghanaian business when he first visited the company 11 years ago to an enterprise operating multiple production lines demonstrated the potential of local businesses when given the opportunity to grow. He noted that the company had expanded its production from line three at the time of his previous visit to line eight, with products serving both the domestic and international markets. President Mahama also encouraged Ghanaian businesses to take advantage of what he described as an improving economic environment to expand production, with investors saying that foreign direct investment (FDI) had increased from $624 million in 2024 to $2.62 billion in 2025, explaining that the development reflected growing confidence in the Ghanaian economy. “If foreigners have confidence in our economy and they are coming and investing, then it means that Ghanaians should also take the opportunity and invest,” he said. The president attributed the improved investment environment to fiscal discipline, efforts to stabilise the economy and measures to create space for the private sector, stating that interest rates had fallen significantly, citing a case in which someone informed him that he had recently obtained financing at nine per cent, compared with rates of about 32 per cent previously. He said the improved economic conditions provided an opportunity for businesses to expand their operations, increase production, and create employment, particularly for young people. The President linked the development of indigenous industries to the government’s 24-hour economy initiative, which seeks to increase production, promote industrialisation and create jobs through additional shifts and expanded economic activity. President Mahama said the growth of companies such as Kasapreko showed that Ghanaian businesses could compete globally when they invested in production, innovation, effective management, and long-term institutional development.

items.title: Mahama congratulates Kasapreko PLC on successful GSE listing
items.description: President John Mahama on Thursday paid a working visit to Kasapreko PLC, commending the Company for its successful listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) Kasapreko PLC on June 15, 2026, officially entered a new chapter in its 38-year journey following its successful listing on the GSE, cementing its position as one of Ghana’s most significant indigenous business success stories. The listing follows a landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO) that attracted approximately GH¢1.72 billion in investor demand, representing a subscription rate of 246 per cent and making it one of the most successful public offers in the recent history of Ghana’s capital market. President Mahama said many Ghanaian companies are afraid to list on the Stock Exchange because they fear that if they do, and others invest in the company, they will lose control of it. “That is not true. Kasapreko has invested, listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange, which is performing very well, and has raised GHC700 million, which it is investing in its new factory at Adeiso,” the President said. “Congratulations on your successful listing, and I am sure that Kasapreko, after the Adeiso factory, will open many more factories, so that is what it is all about, creating jobs for our young people.” President Mahama said it gladdened his heart to visit factories such as Kasapreko and see young people gainfully employed. He said the Government would continue to encourage businesses to invest and expand their operations to create more employment opportunities for Ghanaians. He recalled visiting Kasapreko 11 years ago, when the company was relatively smaller, to inaugurate its Production Line Three. “Today, in this factory alone, they have expanded to Production Line 8, producing all kinds of products, both for the Ghanaian market and for the foreign market,” he said. The President described Kasapreko as a proud Ghanaian brand and a model that other indigenous enterprises could emulate. He said Ghanaian entrepreneurs had the capacity to build successful manufacturing businesses and compete effectively with foreign-owned companies. He said in the past, the assumption was that industry and manufacturing were for Lebanese, Indians and Chinese, and theirs was trade. “We can also invest and do the same thing that everybody else is doing. I always feel proud when I come and see Kasapreko growing in leaps and bounds,” the President said. “We have just seen the new factory that is coming up in Adeiso. I am looking forward to sometime next year when we will have the opportunity to come and commission it, and that is going to add more jobs for our young people.” President Mahama said new industries were emerging under the Government’s 24-Hour Economy initiative, while some existing businesses were expanding production because of what he described as an improved enabling economic environment. “We are exercising fiscal discipline. We are making sure that Government is living within its means and we are creating space for the private sector to grow.” The President said the Government had introduced two key initiatives under its Resetting Ghana Agenda to support industrialisation: the 24-Hour Economy initiative and the Accelerated Export Development Programme, which he chairs. He said the Ministry of Trade had also been redesignated as the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry to broaden its mandate and give greater attention to industrial development. President Mahama said the reorientation of the Ministry had helped to bring industry into focus and given businesses a stronger voice in Government. He commended Mrs Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, Minister of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, for working to bring industry’s concerns and challenges to the Government’s attention for redress.

items.title: La Méditerranée est une mer de plus en plus tropicale
items.description: Depuis la fin du mois de septembre, l'ouest de la Méditerranée est confronté à une intense séquence orageuse qui a provoqué de fortes pluies dans le nord-est de l'Espagne, autour de Barcelone, et dans le sud-est de la France. Plusieurs météorologues estiment que le phénomène, qui a pris une structure tourbillonnaire, pourrait correspondre aux premiers stades d'une formation cyclonique semblable à celles observées dans les régions tropicales. La Méditerranée a déjà connu par le passé des « medicanes », soit des dépressions (des systèmes de basse pression dans lesquels l'air s'élève et génère des nuages, du vent et de la pluie) qui acquièrent des caractéristiques proches de celles des cyclones tropicaux. Or, le phénomène observé début octobre semble différent : il s'agirait plutôt d'un groupe d'orages, soit de l'air chaud et humide qui s'élève rapidement, qui se seraient organisés en un vaste système convectif, au point de former leur propre tourbillon. Selon le météorologue espagnol Juan Jesús González Alemán, « il n’y a pas de précédent de ce type en Méditerranée » Juan Jesús González Alemán : “Todo apunta hacia un ciclón tropical, algo nunca visto en el Mediterráneo” », La Vanguardia , 6 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Sur la vidéo ci-dessus, réalisée par le physicien italien Guido Cioni, on peut distinguer des signes de rotation, qui pourraient correspondre aux premières étapes d'une cyclogenèse tropicale, un processus extrêmement rare en Méditerranée. Cioni estime que ces orages sont à l'origine de la « montagne » de pluie qui s'est abattue entre Barcelone et Marseille du 29 septembre au 5 octobre The Mediterranean is turning into a Tropical Ocean and the storms keep coming », Guido's Weather and Climate Corner, 7 octobre 2026.'> 3 . La station de Saint-Hippolyte-du-Fort, dans le Gard, a enregistré 374 mm de pluie au cours de la semaine, soit l'équivalent de sept mois de précipitations à Paris. Les températures élevées en mer Méditerranée ont vraisemblablement favorisé la formation de ces orages : le 25 septembre, la température moyenne de surface de la Méditerranée dépassait encore 26 °C, une température jamais atteinte aussi tard dans la saison depuis au moins 1991, selon nos calculs à partir des données du service européen Copernicus. Avec le réchauffement climatique, les océans emmagasinent un excès de chaleur qu'ils conservent pendant des périodes prolongées, parfois plusieurs années. Chaque année démarre ainsi avec un surplus de chaleur hérité des précédentes. Au cœur de l'été, la température de la Méditerranée atteint ainsi désormais des pics autour de 28 °C, soit environ 2 degrés de plus que la moyenne 1991-2020. Ces températures sont plus proches de celles des océans tropicaux que de celles des mers situées aux latitudes moyennes, selon Cioni. L’article La Méditerranée est une mer de plus en plus tropicale est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Four Paws expert sees ‘hope’ for ailing elephant Madhubala
items.description: • Dr Amir Khalil says elephant can now stand and walk, but hind-leg problem and significant weight loss remain a concern • Sri Lankan expert likely to arrive today KARACHI: Dr Amir Khalil of Four Paws — an international animal welfare organisation that has been providing support to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) in elephant care for the past several years — has said that ailing elephant Madhubala still “has hope, as her condition has improved”. Dr Khalil, who arrived at the metropolis on Thursday, said this after he made a detailed medical assessment of Madhubala. He and Dr Buddhika Bandara, a prominent Sri Lankan wildlife health specialist and veterinarian, were called in recent days after Safari vets had so far been unable to diagnose the factors behind Madhubala’s ongoing health crisis. Speaking to Dawn about her condition, Dr Khalil said that Madhubala had suffered from multiple infections three weeks ago, but her condition had improved. “Madhubala can stand and walk now, thanks to the efforts over the last three weeks following cooperation with the team on the ground. Still, the situation regarding her hind leg and loss of [significant] weight is critical,” Dr Khalil said, emphasising that a lot needed to be done to improve her condition. “This includes [an] improved diet, administration of required medicines as well as building a treatment crush that provides stress-free access for medical procedures,” he explained, adding that there was still hope for Madhubala. About the infections she had, Dr Khalil said that the initial blood reports showed that she had several bacterial infections while her stool sample indicated a parasitic infection. “She needs to have an intensive treatment programme covering all aspects of recovery.” Sources said Dr Bandara is expected to arrive in Karachi on Friday (today). Both experts have been called in by the KMC after seeing continued deterioration in Madhubala’s condition. She reportedly collapsed twice in her enclosure in recent weeks. The sources said the foreign experts would also examine Malika, Madhubala’s companion. They are the country’s last two captive elephants. It may be recalled that Madhubala had been in solitary confinement at Karachi Zoo following the tragic death of her companion Noor Jehan, who died in 2023 after a tragic fall in her enclosure. Noor Jehan’s autopsy report released by KMC showed that she died from a severe blood parasitic infection and internal trauma combined with a lack of proper medical care. Left alone at the zoo, Madhubala was successfully relocated to Safari Park, where she was reunited with her sisters, Sonia and Malika, in November 2024, under the supervision of Four Paws. The success story of her reunion soon faded as Sonia died a month later after collapsing in her Safari enclosure. Lab reports later showed that she suffered from multiple chronic illnesses, affecting almost all vital organs, indicating prolonged neglect in her care and failure in timely diagnosis. The successive deaths of captive elephants raised public outcry, forcing the KMC to set up an 18-member body last year to look after Madhubala and Malika, both of whom were diagnosed with tuberculosis. The four female elephants had been brought to Karachi from Tanzania in 2010 at a very young age under a controversial arrangement. Published in Dawn, October 9th, 2026

War’s Hidden Mental Health Toll on Children with Disabilities
items.description: Click to expand Image Ibrahim, a 5-year-old boy with autism, is held by his father in Idlib, Syria, June 2022. © © 2022 Human Rights Watch. As armed conflicts proliferate around the globe, World Mental Health Day is a reminder that the psychological toll stemming from hostilities result in mental health harms that have lasting effects on people’s lives. Insecurity, trauma, anxiety, and confusion are the norm for many who have endured armed conflict. Access to services is frequently inadequate—even though over a fifth of conflict-affected populations are estimated to experience mental health conditions such as post-traumatic stress, depression or anxiety. For people, including children, with intellectual disabilities, these harms can be compounded by social, attitudinal, and environmental barriers, which interact with their disability and can heighten their exposure to violence and exclusion. The father of a boy with an intellectual disability in Syria, described in 2020 the effects that the war there had had on his son. The boy, who was 13 at the time, had become increasingly withdrawn and isolated. “He sits alone, doesn’t want to interact with any other kids,” said his father, who also described the psychological distress affecting his other children. “You can see the fear in their eyes. They have no hopes for the future.” Because of communication barriers, a lack of accessible information, and inadequate communication support, people with intellectual and other disabilities are frequently excluded from humanitarian assistance and mental health services, even when such services are available to others affected by the conflict. Human Rights Watch has documented lack of inclusive psychological support for people with disabilities in other armed conflicts, including Gaza and Sudan. Governments should address these gaps by integrating disability-inclusive mental health support during conflict and recovery, in line with their international obligations. Humanitarian agencies providing such services should also take steps to ensure that their programs are disability-inclusive and do not exclude people with disabilities. This could include providing accessible communication methods, such as pictograms and play therapy for children, training staff to provide disability-inclusive support, and equipping them with tactile regulation tools—like weighted lap pads, squeeze balls, and noise-canceling headphones—to help manage sensory overload. Accessible, inclusive mental health care and support are policies that cannot undo the trauma of war, but they can help create the conditions for recovery, inclusion, and hope for the future.

items.title: Capital Development Authority plans to execute 11th Avenue project in two phases
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) is planning to execute the 11th Avenue project in two phases, starting the first phase from E-11 to Srinagar Highway. Recently, CDA’s DWP approved PC-I worth Rs24.5 billion for the construction of the highway from Margalla Avenue to IJP Road. According to the PC-I, the 7.5km road, with three lanes on each side, will be completed within a year. Officials of the engineering wing said around 17 bridges and overpasses were part of the project. However, sources said that now CDA has decided to execute 11th Avenue in two phases. In first priority phase, the 3.5km road will be constructed from E-11 interchange to Srinagar Highway, including an interchange at Srinagar Highway. DWP recently approved PC-I worth Rs24.5 billion for construction of highway from Margalla Avenue to IJP Road “Recently, during a meeting it was decided that this project will be carried out in two phases. Hopefully, the project will be formally started within two months as currently we are working on pre-tendering process,” said an engineer of CDA. He said that when this phase will be completed, Srinagar Highway will be connected with Margalla Avenue and overall traffic load will be divided on both Margalla Road and Srinagar Highway. To a query, the engineer said that overall PC-I worth Rs24.5 billion had been approved, so “I guess for this portion of 3.5km with an interchange roughly Rs11 to 12 billion will be earmarked. This is a guesswork as proper working is in progress,” he said. It is relevant to note here that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, during his first stint, had laid the foundation stone of 11th Avenue in June 2023, but the project was not started. The avenue is supposed to start from IJP ll allRoad and after passing between I-10 and I-11, G-10, G-11, F-10 and F-11, culminate at the E-11 interchange. From E-11 to D-12, a portion of the road has already been completed and is known as Iran Avenue. After the construction of 9th Avenue decades ago, the CDA could not construct any major road. Work on the construction of 10th Avenue was started in 2022, but after completion of around 50pc of the work, the project was halted last year. CDA officials told Dawn that besides focusing on 11th Avenue, the authority should also complete the stalled 10th Avenue project, as the structure of the incomplete road was deteriorating. They said 10th Avenue was a federally funded project and, due to the non-release of funds, it had been left abandoned. The officials said the CDA had requested the federal government several times for release of fund, but to no avail. According to the CDA, the total cost of the 10th Avenue project was Rs10.2 billion, but the government had released only around Rs4 billion. That was why the project was halted, they said. They said that under the original plan, the project should have been completed by December 2024, but the federal government did not allocate any funds for the public welfare project in its 2024-25 and 2025-26 budgets. On the other hand, earthwork and structure from I.J.P to H-9 have been decaying and also causing inconvenience for public. The officials said with little funding, at least this portion could be brought under use with asphalt work. Published in Dawn, October 9th, 2026

Con un Frente Amplio que incluyera a Podemos, la izquierda alternativa subiría del 7,6% que obtiene por separado al 9,5% y amortiguaría el golpe, aunque siempre lejos de sus resultados de 2023 y sin amenazar la mayoría absoluta del bloque derechista. El problema es mío, por supuesto, ya que la casi totalidad de la humanidad sabe de qué le están hablando o utiliza continuamente esas cosas que al parecer son obligatorias para vivir o para sobrevivir. Son las redes sociales, los WhatsApps, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook... Cosas que al parecer son tan necesarias como comer y dormir. Y recurriendo a una expresión surrealista de otra época que siempre me hizo gracia, me siento en ese universo tan perdido como un pulpo en un garaje. Entre los accesorios se encontraban un bozal y un collar sujeto a un candado. En alguna de las imágenes también posaba dentro de una jaula, participando en un encuentro íntimo a cuatro patas. La letrada explicó que, al ser Gallant amigo del dueño de la tienda de ropa bondage Mr. S Leather, participó en una sesión que pretendía ser “divertida y personal, con el entendimiento de que Mr. S podría usar algunas imágenes en relación con ciertos productos”. items.title: Bella Hadid, la ‘top model’ que se atreve a denunciar la parte más fea del mundo desde su Instagram, cumple 30 años
items.description: Cuando la supermodelo Bella Hadid vino al mundo en Washington, justo hoy hace 30 años, lo hizo en un entorno privilegiado. Su padre, Mohamed Hadid , un promotor inmobiliario de origen palestino que antes de llegar a Estados Unidos estuvo refugiado en Siria, y su madre, Yolanda Hadid , exmodelo holandesa con cierta proyección mediática gracias a un reality show , reunieron una fortuna como para criarla entre un rancho en Santa Bárbara y una mansión en Malibú. Allí, junto a sus hermanos (la también famosa modelo Gigi Hadid y un varón más joven que ellas, Anwar Hadid), creció rodeada de naturaleza y protegida por la armadura invisible del sueño americano, que aún le auguraba un futuro mejor. A la top model , una de las mejor pagadas del mundo, con un patrimonio actual estimado entre los 25 y los 30 millones de dólares, le esperaba, efectivamente, una vida de lujo, de fama y de contratos millonarios con firmas internacionales (Marc Jacobs, Chanel, Givenchy...). En 2014, con 17 años, debutó en la semana de la moda de Nueva York desfilando para Desigual; en 2016, con 20, lo hizo en el icónico desfile de Victoria’s Secret. Pronto dejó de estar a la sombra de su hermana Gigi, un año mayor que ella, y le fue tan bien sobre las pasarelas y en campañas de publicidad que en 2024 pudo pausar su carrera e irse a vivir a la tranquila Texas con su pareja de entonces (el cowboy mexicano Adán Bañuelos) y lanzar su propia colección de fragancias. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Queridos abuelos: soy español y no me dejan votar
items.description: El título podría ser el encabezamiento de una carta imaginaria dirigida por un nieto o una nieta a sus ascendientes exiliados a causa del golpe militar del 18 de julio de 1936, desde esa fecha y hasta el 31 de diciembre de 1955. La norma que concede la nacionalidad española a estas personas aparece, por primera vez, en la Ley de Memoria Histórica de 26 de diciembre de 2007. En su exposición de motivos se propugna la restitución de los que padecieron injusticias y agravios como los que, empujados a un largo, desgarrador y en tantos casos irreversible exilio. La disposición adicional séptima reconoce el derecho a optar por la nacionalidad española a los nietos de los que tuvieron que renunciar a ella como consecuencia del exilio. Los recursos procesales que se presentaron superaron las barreras y no existieron obstáculos para su aplicación. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tamo y sus cinco hijas, a la búsqueda de refugio en el barrio de El Príncipe tras llegar a nado a Ceuta
items.description: Las casitas del humilde barrio de El Príncipe están pintadas con colores intensos. Hay verdes, grises, rosas, azuladas... Todas forman un entramado de callejuelas estrechas que confluyen en varias plazas y de las que sobresalen los minaretes de las mezquitas. Ahora, en sus rincones se resguardan decenas de migrantes que llegaron con la entrada masiva a Ceuta y que no quieren retornar a Marruecos. Algunos llevan solo unos días asentados en el vecindario: son migrantes que vienen de El Trampolín huyendo de la Policía tras el reciente desalojo del asentamiento instalado en la playa . Otros dormitan en las calles o se cobijan en sus casitas de colores ya desde el inicio de la crisis. Entre quienes se han internado en El Príncipe se encuentra Tamo, una mujer marroquí de 35 años, y sus cinco hijas pequeñas. Todas entraron juntas a nado a la ciudad autónoma a finales de julio. Hoy buscan refugio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La urna y la huelga
items.description: El impacto del desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal en la política y la sociedad españolas es aún imprevisible en sus dimensiones, y más después de fallecer este miércoles en el hospital sin haber podido regresar a su casa , tras dos semanas ingresada con un cuadro de ansiedad y fatiga. Una consecuencia directa de esta tragedia es la huelga general convocada por los sindicatos mayoritarios para el 11 de noviembre, dos días antes del comienzo de la campaña electoral para los comicios del día 29. Los grandes sindicatos de clase se han sumado a una movilización social iniciada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas, una organización al margen del ámbito laboral con apenas 3.000 miembros que ha logrado, con la acampada en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid, condicionar por completo la agenda política en España. La del 11-N será la novena huelga general en democracia . Y, por primera vez, no tiene su origen en recortes sociales o laborales. La convocatoria responde a un malestar social que pivota en torno a la crisis de la vivienda, y que ha sido galvanizado por las manifestaciones y acampadas pacíficas de las últimas dos semanas. Seguir leyendo

Es el caso de estos calamares de campo, que de calamares no tienen nada, pero recuerdan a ellos por su elaboración y su forma. Se preparan con cebolla y pimiento, se pasan por harina y se fríen en aceite. Muy simple y muy efectivo: quedan crujientes y jugosos, y los comerás como si fuesen pipas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Economic Coordination Committee raises duty on tyre, bike parts import
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government on Thursday increased additional customs duty (ACD) on import of tyres and motorcycle parts produced locally and approved first-loss coverage for small and medium enterprises and small farmers. The decisions were taken at a meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet, presided over by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb. The committee also approved investment of Export Development Fund (EDF) resources in government securities and allowed Rs57.85 billion in supplementary grants a day after a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and at the conclusion of the first quarter of the fiscal year. Under the decision, the government increased ACD from 4pc to 11pc on import of radial tyres and motorcycle parts that are manufactured locally. It also increased ACD from 11pc to 31pc on motorbike parts imported by local manufacturers. Both measures are aimed at facilitating local manufacturers of radial tyres and motorcycle parts. “On a summary submitted by the Revenue Division, the ECC approved an amendment to SRO 693(I)/2006 concerning the levy of additional customs duty on import of tyres being manufactured locally. The measure is aimed at promoting domestic manufacturing,” an official statement said. The ECC also approved a financing framework developed by the State Bank of Pakistan to facilitate the inclusion of Agency Financial Institutions (AFIs) under the government’s existing Risk Coverage Schemes for Small Enterprises and Small Farmers through wholesale and agency arrangements. The framework provides for first-loss coverage to loans up to 20pc for SMEs and 10pc each to small farmers and medium size industries. “The framework aims to broaden access to finance by leveraging the outreach of eligible microfinance and non-banking financial institutions,” the statement added. The ECC also approved an Addendum to the Second Supplemental Trust Deed of the Credit Guarantee Trust Fund (CGTF), originally meant for Prime Minister’s Mera Pakistan Mera Ghar scheme, expanding its scope to facilitate more effective utilisation of the existing credit guarantee facility to support affordable housing finance. The meeting approved 11 supplementary grants totalling Rs57.85bn. These included Rs2bn for the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority to facilitate implementation of its approved business plan in line with the prime minister’s vision. It also approved another Rs11.329bn for the Industries and Production Division to meet the immediate funding requirements of the Utility Stores Corporation and facilitate completion of its closure process. On the request of the Privatisation Division, the ECC approved Rs8bn for the Public Private Partnership Authority (P3A) to support the development and implementation of infrastructure projects through public-private partnerships. The meeting also approved a Rs10bn grant for the Ministry of Railways to provide budgetary cover for the Thar Coal Rail Connectivity Project and facilitate the utilisation of indigenous Thar coal for power generation and other industrial sectors. Published in Dawn, October 9th, 2026

items.title: Opposition leaders booked over protests in India
items.description: NEW DELHI: Police on Thur­sday registered an FIR against opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, Congress lawmaker Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several others for allegedly forcing their way into the Akashvani Bhavan premises during a Tuesday protest, The Hindu reported. The FIR followed the detention of about 260 people, including 10 lawmakers, after an opposition INDIA bloc march from parliament toward the Election Commission of India. Police said protesters breached barricades and ignored orders to disperse. On Wednesday, the Congress party accused police of using “brute force” to briefly detain the Gandhis and other lawmakers heading to New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest site. Police dismissed the claims as an effort to “defame” the force. “We are on the ground and, as officers, we also ensure that every kind of legal duty is followed and no illegal, unnecessary actions take place,” senior police officer Shrishti Pandey told the ANI news agency. Congress lawmaker Imran Masood denied any forcible entry, noting other lawmakers accompanied Rahul Gandhi. “They should not be mistaken that we will back off fearing an FIR,” Masood said, adding that authorities refused to meet them. “Now we will go and sit in front of their houses.” Demonstrations entered a third day on Thursday as opposition parties, student groups and the “Cockroach” youth movement demanded Chief Election Commi­ssioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Protesters accuse Prime Mini­ster Nar­endra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Par­ty of rigging voter lists in collusion with Ku­mar. Kumar has not commented, while the commission and the BJP denied the allegations. Published in Dawn, October 9th, 2026

items.title: Iran weighs US response as Trump rules out attack before midterms
items.description: • Araghchi says Tehran can reply to proposal within days; Iranian atomic chief vows not to give up enrichment • Centcom terms Hormuz closure claims ‘false’ TEHRAN: Iran announced on Thursday that it was still reviewing Washington’s response to a proposal under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within seven days, as US President Donald Trump indicated that he will not attack Iran before November’s midterm elections amid ‘productive talks’. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran could reply within days, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency, emphasising that “the diplomatic process is still continuing”. Trump wrote on Truth Social that Washington will not strike Iran prior to the Nov 3 midterm elections, calling talks with Tehran “productive”. “I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition … we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on Nov 3,” Trump wrote. Meanwhile, Trump said that his special envoy Steve Witkoff is “doing very well” in negotiations with Iran, though he indicated that an agreement is not his preferred outcome, Anadolu reported. “He’s working on the Iran deal and doing very well. I think the deal isn’t really something that I want to do, but they’re willing to offer us anything to stop,” Trump told supporters at a campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas, adding that Tehran “will never have a nuclear weapon”. Trump described Witkoff as “a great negotiator” who has “done some phenomenal things”, citing the ceasefire deal in Gaza, and said he expects the war with Iran to end soon. “That war ends — it’s going to be very soon. It’s got to be very soon,” Trump said, descr­ibing Iran as “a failed nation”. He also reiterated his claim that Iran has been defeated “economically and militarily” and said the US naval blockade will remain in place, while claiming that oil is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz in “record numbers” with 22 million barrels passing through Wednesday night. Despite the ongoing talks, Iran will not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium, state media reported Thursday, citing Mohammad Eslami, the head of Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation. Dismissing renewed US threats aga­inst Iran’s nuclear facilities as “nothing new”, he said enrichment was “an inseparable part” of the nuclear process. On the aviation front, the first commercial flight operated by a foreign airline to fly into Iran since the outbreak of the Middle East war landed on Thursday, state media repo­rted, after the United States granted a sanctions waiver for Iraq’s national carrier. The waiver applies to pilgr­ims travelling between Iran and Najaf, alongside a separate agreement allowing Iran­ian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate daily flights on the route. At sea, Maj Gen Ahmad Vahidi, commander-in-chief of the IRGC, warned that military forces are ready “with crushing weapons to deliver a decisive response to any attempt at unauthorised passage in the Strait of Hormuz,” Fars reported. US Central Comm­and rejected Iranian claims that the waterway is closed. However, shipping data from analytics firm Kpler showed the number of vessels transiting the strait fell to seven on Tuesday, the lowest in more than two months, before edging up to 10 on Wednesday, after tanker attacks reached a wartime high last week. “Crude crossing the strait fell 27 per cent from a wartime high the week before, to at least 10.1 million barrels a day,” Kpler analysts Emma­nuel Belostrino and Yui Torikata wrote Tuesday, though rising exports from the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea kept overall Middle East crude exports at pre-war levels. Published in Dawn, October 9th, 2026

Meanwhile, Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani on Thursday expressed serious concerns over the sharp rise in terrorist incidents in KP, insisting that the province had increasingly turned into a war zone while alleging that the provincial government was fai­ling to play its due role in combating terrorism, APP reported. Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam on Thursday urged the KP government to focus on resolving public issues instead of pursuing a protest march. items.title: Saudis reel from attacks as allies debate ‘involvement’
items.description: • Houthis fire missiles at Riyadh airport, airbases; kindergarten, clinic complex damaged by debris • Lufthansa, Air India suspend flights to Saudi capital; half of all departures cancelled • Nothing in Makkah pact bars members from joining Yemen fight, says Kh Asif • Ankara calls accord ‘purely defensive’, rules out sending troops; Syria weighs deployment RIYADH: Yemen’s Houthi forces escalated their campaign against Saudi Arabia on Thursday, attempting to shut down the kingdom’s airspace and oil facilities with missile fire that disrupted flights and damaged a kindergarten and medical complex. Lufthansa and Air India said on Thursday they will suspend flights to Riyadh as the Yemeni group renewed threats against airlines, after claiming a third attack on King Khalid International Airport. According to data compiled by aviation analytics company Cirium, 49.7pc of departures from Riyadh airport had been cancelled by 1500 GMT, with 31 more cancellations expected for Friday across all Saudi airports. Flight tracker FlightRadar24 also showed numerous delayed arrivals and departures. The airport did not acknowledge the disruption, pointing only to the “necessity” of contacting airlines before travelling. A thick black column of smoke and flames rose from Riyadh airport in a video verified by Reuters . A witness and three people briefed on the matter said a stationary commercial plane had caught fire and caused the smoke, though the fire was later put out. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched two ballistic missiles at Riyadh’s airport, one at an airport in Najran and another at an airbase in Khamis Mushait. Saree also ordered workers at Saudi oil facilities to evacuate days after the group hit a major refinery south of the capital. Around the same time, the Saudi-led coalition said it had destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh and another toward Khamis Mushait. Shortly after, Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency posted on X that “interception debris” had fallen in Riyadh, causing material damage to a kindergarten and a medical clinic complex, without specifying if there were any casualties. After loud booms echoed across Riyadh on Thursday morning, several multinational firms in the King Abdullah Financial District told staff to work from home or evacuated employees, according to people familiar with the matter. Diplomats were instructed to shelter in place at their embassies, and at least one international school sent children into a basement for safety. Defence pact As Saudi Arabia pushes for allied support to reverse Houthi gains, regional states are weighing their involvement under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. Following an emergency alliance meeting in Riyadh earlier this week, members have agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities in the kingdom. But while both Ankara and Islamabad have pledged support for Riyadh, Turkish and Pakistani officials offered contrasting interpretations on Thursday regarding whether the pact is strictly limited to territorial defence, or permits direct military involvement. In Turkiye, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan ruled out sending troops to confront the Houthis. “This is a defence agreement,” he said. “If one of the countries is attacked, you support its defence. This is not an offensive agreement.” Turkiye “will not send its troops to another country’s territory to launch an attack,” he stressed. Meanwhile in Pakistan, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told ARY News on Thursday that no stipulation in the Makkah pact bars alliance members from getting “directly involved” if one member faced a threat. “To defend one of the member countries, the remaining two would get involved as if they were defending themselves,” Mr Asif said, though he separately told Geo News that while Pakistan and Turkiye had a “presence in the theatre”, only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations. Separately, the Ministry of Information on Thursday dismissed a New York Times report claiming Pakistan Air Force aircraft were being used against the Houthis as “fake and fabricated”, having earlier termed a Reuters report claiming the deployment of 30,000 to 40,000 Pakistani troops as “speculative”. “International media houses are again asked to avoid speculative reporting with regards to employment of Pakistan’s military forces under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” it added. Meanwhile, Damascus is also said to be considering options for military support, including defensive aid for Saudi Arabia or an offensive deployment against the Houthis, according to US and Syrian defence officials. “Should Saudi Arabia request any military cooperation or exchange of expertise, this would take place exclusively through official channels and within the framework of the bilateral agreements governing relations between our two brotherly countries,” the diplomat said. On Thursday, oil prices jumped more than five per cent, then pared gains after President Donald Trump said the US will not launch an attack on Iran before midterm congressional elections in November. Brent crude futures were up $3.48, or 3.5pc, at $103.73 a barrel by 1641 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $2.69, or 3.1pc, to $91. Published in Dawn, October 9th, 2026
